text: Good game, plenty of content with a good roaster of units. I really like this game however, it is not a very giving game. sadly one of the least giving phone games i have played. what is a real shame. getting currency for pull on units is far between and can feel like they are trying to back you in a corner to pay to win, along with mixing resources and units in the same pulls. I would give it a 5 star if it was not for that. very frustrating.

Potentially interesting tactical game. Unfortunately, it's a boring grindfest. After a certain point it becomes impossible to progress, unless you repetitively play the same mission over and over, or pay hundreds(!!!) of quid to unlock upgrades. It's insane. I want to play the game, but it won't let me unless I grind???

One of the better mobile games about. its well made and has lots of events to keep you busy. The only downside is the price they charge for in game items, I wouldn't give them a penny. Its laughable what they try to charge. Surly reasonable prices would lead to more in game purchases? Im not going to spend the price of a PS5 for a laughable amount of in game items.

Well, gave this game a second run and with me getting removed from a guild because the chat box doesn't work (won't allow me to enter a typed message). Here's my thoughts on it. If you don't spend money, progress falls to a stand still where you can't go past a certain point in the campaign because you're extremely under level. I truly don't understand what youtubers are talking about when they say this is a "Authentic Warhammer experience".

Unless you are in the mood to watch endless adds and pay a shi! load of money, this game is not for you. It is surprising that a company as recognised as Warhammer (They have existed longer than I have been alive) is reliant on addstoturn a profit. This is even more surprising considering the exorbitant costs to purchase anything in the game. In summary if you enjoy warhammer, and are comfortable spending hundreds of dollars every month just to be competitive then this is the game for you.

I wouldn't call it pay to win, but pay to skip the grind. You make progress quickly as the gacha system works in your favour at the beginning, but then it gives you 10 shards for a character that needs 500 and you realise it's going to be a long grind. Once you've unlocked your characters, you need more shards to level them up, then orbs to upgrade their rarity to continue leveling up. You also need loot to upgrade their rank. It takes a lot to make decent progress, but the gameplay is fun.

great game! the gameplay is smooth, easy to learn but hard to master, and the fact that every character has a name is useful for me, as i have some great names I can steal in case I ever want to bring a named character from that faction to my collection. I personally think that, if you buy a model and they are in tacticus, you could get a special one-use code to get that model in tacticus, or a fallback like Blackstone or an upgrade if you already have them

For a mobile game, this one is actually very good. Slowly developing your roster over time is very satisfying, though it's a marathon rather than a sprint. It doesn't force you to spend money, and the devs listen to the players' feedback - the recent overhaul of the Onslaught game mode is much appreciated, and, though infrequent, the character rebalancing breathes life into underperforming units.

I give 4 stars because I'm a fan of Warhammer 40k Game, itself, is very long [if you want to high achievements (couple years)] or very expensive if you want your progress fast. Is highly enjoyable but gets monotonous at some point. as a fan I recommend it. !!! as "normal" gamer is up to you what you like but as long term game this one is pretty cheap

I'm now addicted. It seemed a lot to take in at first but I am tarnished from a few other over complicated RPGs. The learning curve is acceptable and gameplay is fun. The character development and story is simple but better than a lot of others I have played due to this. Simple but done right. Excited to see how this develops. Been playing for three hours now! Might be a late night for me tonight!

I kind of expected more from a Warhammer game, but it's ok just not what I was looking for. I hope they make a turn based game with dice and all the miniatures models and tanks from the real Warhammer models played exactly like the real life table top game in scenarios against the computer and other players with fully paintable figures and all the different armies to collect, so people can work out which models work well in battle and which ones are worth buying and collecting in real life.

It's a good game, but when the game there is also a difficulty curve at a point. , the token system sucks, especially with how long it takes to gain ONE out of the TWO you can even use.you also need a lot of luck for requisition pulls, for there garenteed characters pull if you have 10, but it's of any character and it has a high chance of a character that'll only give you 20 shards while everything else isn't good. I've played since the 2nd anniversary and never drew a legendary from a pull.

Basic pay-to-win lootboxer. A shame really because a lot of time and energy has gone into making it as tempting to spend money as possible, and yet, with a fraction of that effort they could have added some much more enjoyable gameplay and strategy. As it is, this game is a very basic grinding game, dressed up very nicely. The developers are clearly talented but were only interested in exploiting players, not delivering anything of merit.

It's a fun little time waster. Has some varied mechanics ticking along under the hood and a ever growing roster of a seemingly endless supply of characters from the 40k universe. However after a promising start where you will meet little challenge, you hit the barrier of difficulty and endless packs offering the opportunity to pay to progress. The game is VERY expensive. VERY, and even paying out the £'s only gives random items, thus you may not even get what you require. Buyerbeware.

Simple and fun for the most part! Perhaps lacking a little in complexity for my taste. However, I feel as though the monetization of the product is predatory and unnecessary. Had you included, say, a premium version which was paid, featured no ads, had increased acquisition rates for in game currency and unclocked more characters immidiately, I would have been inclined to pay! It demonstrates a lack of faith in the game as a whole, that you feel the need to have such a poor monetization model

Same as every other game on this platform, filled to the brim with predatory mechanics to try and get as much money from you as possible. Battle passes, different currencies, energy limits, can only replay levels a short number of times, (don't want you getting the gear you need straight away), needing large numbers of shards to get the characters you want, and only dropping very small amounts in the lootboxes. This game is not for you to enjoy it's for you to empty your bank.

I was enjoying the game. Playing for a couple of months, which seems to be the point when most players hit the same wall. Levelling up characters to progress with increasingly expensive upgrades costs two, sometimes three separate currencies. Do Raid Credits really need to exist when you already have to spend precious energy to do this? You're at the mercy of a really poor Gacha system when it comes to unlocking characters as it is. The gameplay is fun, but lazy monetization kills it dead.

As a fan of 40k and of games like this I've got to say I'm hugely disappointed. The gameplay itself is fun and seems reasonably balanced. That's where the good news ends though. The games progression is excruciatingly slow. You spend the first day in the game going through mission after mission before hitting a brick wall. That brick wall is the games appalling economy. The game basically forces you to pay (insane prices) to be able to progress at all. Sadly it's unplayable in this state

Edit: Changed rating from 3* to 1*. It's literally impossible to advance without spending money at a certain point. I am stuck on mission 55, the enemies are "Very hard" and I get 1 shot by each of them. The equipment I need to upgrade my characters is locked behind mission 64 which is impossible to get to without buying OP characters from the store. I can't even level my characters to make them stronger that way as your level is locked behind the rarity of the character.

Very much pay to win. You won't realise at first as it gives the impression you'll be able to win fights and it throws lots of items at you for free in the early stages. After a while it hits a wall in difficulty which results in needing to buy items to progress. Personally, I'd rather you added adverts and didn't try to fool people or offered the game as a one off fee and again, didn't try to fool people with the 'free' price tag.

Great game, got a lot of depth. However the grind aspect is very limited. You can't keep playing to catch up with people who are very established so it's harder for new players and a barrier to entry. My recommendation is to have energy, onslaught tokens and salvage tokens done per faction rather than universal. This allows for more play time and will be particularly helpful to new players.

As a lot of people have said, the gameplay is good, but they is a super HARD! Pay wall in the game where if you don't pay, you can't really get the full experience of it. For example, to do the next campaigns, you'll have to have a full set of 3 characters, but!! you'll be missing one in all of them, and the price for each of them is like £10, £14 and £14 which is a joke.. for the level of money you'll be putting into it, it'll be cheaper to actually get the models themselves.

Not a bad game, the big issue I have is the amount of systems they use to get money out of you. I understand you have to for the studio to survive but limiting the player with energy never feels right, I'm not bothered that it's going to take time and effort to get X character but why stop my from playing? The gameplay is good and the game loop is decent. But just wish I could play more ... O wait I can play more, I just have to spend real world money.

The game itself is great at its base. But seriously, stop playing scummy game with the lootbox system. Just spent a lot of time grinding trying to get special requisitions to hopefully increase my odds, only to find out that they all disappeared without notice, none of them opened. This doesn't even get into the fact that the odds of getting anything have been seeningly getting worse and worse. Stop punishing me trying to play the game

I quit this game a year ago because of some progression and pay wall issues, but i picked it back up a couple weeks ago. They seem to have fixed a lot of that, and I've been enjoying the game a great deal since. My only real gripe is the matchmaking in arena mode are incredibly lopsided, and a new player has basically no hope of winning any significant number of matches. That's really busted, but other than that, it's been a good time!

Terribly pay to win. Basically everything you'd expect from a company with BlackRock as shareholders : low returns for those who use it, coupled with a need to keep ploughing in cash in order to keep up with even mid level players. The packs are expensive for very little return; the in-game currencies likewise. It's nice to play as your favourite characters from the game, but after more than a week of casual play you'll be hard pressed to gain any sort of footing without a large bank account.

Fun but microtransactions are out of control. $35 to buy a pack that contains the materials to unlock a character 20% of the way is absolutely insane. So $175 to fully unlock ONE character. The drops are rigged and almost always repeat the characters you already have. The gameplay is fun, but the developers are insanely greedy. You'd have to spend hundreds if not thousands to be competitive in the game. All of the events cater to high level players and leave you with few rewards for playing.

If they spent as much time on the gameplay as they did monetization, this could have been a good game. As it stands, it sucks. Some missions you cannot win without levelling up your character, which typically means finding one of the dozen or so different currencies. I have no idea why they decided we needed gold, orbs, shards, tokens, cards, scrap, items, tickets, training points, xp, requisition points... I'm not even exaggerating.

I enjoy playing this game quite a bit, but you can only play it for about 10 minutes per day due to how they have set up the energy system. You run out of energy extremely quick, then you can only do 2 salvage runs, and 3 of wave based battle. It's fun, but incredibly frustrating when shortly after opening the app, there is nothing you can do. Why make it take 12 hours for one salvage token? Why make it take 35 minutes for 1 battle worth of energy? Ridiculous.

Decent game let down by greed. Quickly find yourself stuck and needing power ups and supplies but due to the ridiculously low number of attempts for the various farming modes and equally unnecessary recharge times you'll find yourself struggling to even be able to do anything for a while UNLESS you pay. Yes, they need to make money, but if you don't have the money to waste or don't want to spend, it's pretty easy to get super bored real quick. Shame.

This is a good game but it is let down by a few points. The battle pass is really not worth it, many of the missions just not possible with early characters and it takes so long to complete that it sucks all the fun out of the game - i played loads and only onlocked ½ the tokens for the character. Gameplay is good if a little repetitive. Arena mode often puts you up against foes you can't beat. Graphics means you often can't distinguish pathing which is really frustrating. Otherwise it's good!

Been playing for around 2 years. It's fun but extremely grindy. The big issue now though is that it feels like the devs are pushing the game even further into pay-to-win territory. It's always been pretty pay to win, but they've been making events less and less completable without paying for extra tries, regardless of how strong your own characters are.

It's my first time playing with this game. I enjoy it quite a lot. It reminds me of the Star Wars one but more like chess. The 40K universe I have been getting into for the last few years and to find something on mobile I like very much. It plays well, runs smooth, and has lots of options for characters and stats.

So far it's a promising game as someone relatively new to Warhammer. Offers some decent challenges and thinking, but could be a little more optimised for lower end devices (or add a graphics setting). That's my only gripe so far. Please keep expanding the roster, of course. Emperor guide you, Snowprint.

This game is cool, but it suffers from excessive monetization of its content. Once you hit a certain point, like power level 15, it's very hard to progress at a semi decent rate. This game tries to force you to pay in order to complete game events or to make some progress that isn't just bare minimum allowed. if you don't pay, it's a slog to get characters unlocked, leveled and powered up. I doubt it, but if they came down from the overuse of monetizing everything, this game would be perfect.

game is okay but lacks the complexity promised considering the lack of units and scale the player is able to control. events seem rewarding and store is not too predatory. However, their privacy policy is apparently either false, loopholed, or even worse, they've got a breach. I've signed up for nothing else, and yet, I've suddenly started recieving mass sales calls. 4 in the last hour in fact.

Very fun warhammer experience that I can take with me wherever. A lot of continual enjoyment, and of course great vibes and aesthetic. Only issue is you'll probably hit a point where you'll feel like you have to spend money to either get better or actaully get the characters you want. Character reward shards are very slow to receive, but it does make you want to keep playing. Overall, one of my favorite mobile games (largely because it IS warhammer).

This game started out awesome and a ton of fun with lots to do but very quickly became just another one of those games where you have to pay money to progress at a reasonable pace and actually have things to do. a couple weeks into the game and I already have hit walls where I cant power up quick enough to have more than 10 minutes of game time a day and the only way to speed it up is to spend money. There's also certain campaigns where you have to pay money just to unlock them....

The usual cash grab with a Warhammer skin: the app pretends that your skill and strategy matter before hitting you with a "pay to win" wall that comes quick and hard after only a couple of hours. And that app is VERY expensive. It is going nowhere without a deep wallet. I did not even bother with a guild. Visually average but rapidly unplayable. Just don't.

The visuals are great, the game is fun for only a few weeks before being a chore, the game is unbalanced in a way that makes progress go as slow as possible, with little to no reward after even weeks of daily playing. The game is very clearly tailored to get the most money as possible, and its a shame seeing the true passion that must have gone into game, campaigns so perfectly crafted to lore, orks play fast and aggressive, there are other things I can't fit. All in all, greedy, with no reward

Excellent strategy game. I enjoy the large amount of content, quests and rewards, leveling characters and getting new equipment. I greatly appreciate that in game purchases are really not needed to level or unlock characters, as you progress with regular play at a good pace. If you are in a hurry I can see the benefit. The battle pass is not expensive (I think about $5) and more than worth it to support the game and developers.

Talk about relying on brand recognition. I have never seen a more stingy game. I don't mind throwing some money into a game if it is fun, but this is barely a game. Mediocre art assets, and pretty much a guarantee that you can only play the starting characters if you don't pay money. Blackstone, the currency in the game, shows up in crates or from missions. I have yet to see one that gives more than 7, and it takes 300 to MAYBE get a piece of a character you don't have. Inexcusable.

Cool mechanics, could have been lots of fun. Very, very pay to win. Constant pressure to purchase. Pop-ups that cover the entire screen pressuring you to buy (or go to the newer Taxticus website and buy) interfere with the gameplay and take the fun out of it. Unlocking a character is about $25. It's really just a series of super expensive pay walls. Again, too bad, because there's a cool game underneath there somewhere, just impossible to find that game thru the paywall any more.

This game is fun in the beginning but quickly turns into an egregiously long and tedious grind to make any noticeable progress. The alternative, sink hundreds maybe thousands of dollars into the chance of getting premium characters that are basically unavailable to the F2P base. These premium characters are all you see in competitive game modes. You can't beat them, the mechanics are broken, you just have to bend over and take it without complaining. It's infuriating

I really do love playing this app, but I hate energy to play systems, it takes 6 energy to play one level of a campaign mission, you get 1 every 5 minutes... it takes half an hour to play once. it has a lot of game modes and events to play that don't think energy, but they still take coins and those take actual hours to come back for the most part. there's one that comes back every 15 minutes, but still.

I love anything Warhammer and this game is a lot of fun. No learning curve to speak of, and not terribly challenging as yet. I've just been playing a short time, so no doubt that will change as you proceed and level up. A lot of "battle" games stress the #@&* out of me LOL, but this one...you can just sit back, relax and play.

game's pretty mid The tutorial takes about hour and a half to do and you have to do the entire first tutorial campaign with units that you'll never give a f*** about after you get the army you actually want to use. on top of that say I want to play works well great that's seven campaigns away from me being able to play as them. If you like the universe that's only worth a few stars but the games is just hollow.

I've only known bits and pieces about the universe of Warhammer 40K since the '80s and I know that I cannot afford to play it. However, I love the lore. Thought this might be a fun way to learn about it. I like strategy games on phones and stuff anyways. I can see where they'll probably be a paywall or something eventually, but I'm enjoying it at the moment.

I'm bumping it to a 4. I enjoy the gameplay, it is definitely a marathon grind. However there are SO MANY MTXs shoved in your face, AND an entirely different shop outside of the game to buy even more stuff. Feels extremely predatory. And that is on top of optional ads for extra energy and other stuff, which are limited, not to mention pretty bad energy economy that doing the energy one feels mandatory.

I have never played a game that does NOT want you to play it this much. it is INSANE how much this game shoots you in the foot every time you turn around. Most F2P mobile games are heavily monetized and have a bunch of different currencies, but Tacticus is on another level. EVERYTHING has 20 currencies that all interact with each other, and but you only earn 1 energy every 5 minutes, it takes 5-6 energy to do anything. I can't even progress the main story at this point. Couldn't give them my $

I seems you can obtain everything if you play with infinite time. As time is finite, the paywall is steep for basic functionnalities like obtaining champions or playing a campaing. You'll pay the price of several triple A game to obtain everything. That's just a loss of timr and money not worth the efforts --> Uninstall.

I love the game and the characters are very detailed and nicely designed however I do have one suggestion and it is where when you go into your collection it would be nice if there was a way you can see your total power. Otherwise, the game is magnificent and very intriguing there are some minor details that I would like, (including this one) but it's a great game overall. Thank you for this great opportunity in becoming close to Warhammer. 😊

Downloaded cause I got a code from Warhammer+ and thought I'd give it a try. App runs fine. It's just candy crush for Warhammer nerds. I thought I outgrew gaming. But it was "pay to win" schemes that just ruined the fun for me. This "game" is no different. Seriously. $30 player packs, that's not including the $3-$10 "micro" transactions. Strategy means nothing compared to a kid who has stolen his parents' credit card info.

It says my information was deleted from the servers and it would take reinstallation to play again. I've done that 5 times and it gives the same pop up with no way out. I just want my account I've put money into. Edit* the team got back to me and got the issue resolved! Their customer support was great!

Great game as far as the UI and leveling up but a core mechanic of the game I was most interested in is completely screwed up. The guild war mechanic is great and fun but the nerf is crazy. Why waste time and effort upgrading to get nerfed to the point of base level characters? Why punish the people who spent time and effort into the game? Doesnt make sense because they wanna give the lower levels a "chance". If you wanna give them a chance, put them against people who are similar level.

the game would fun but it's horrifically expensive, unironically more expensive than the table top game. Outdated concepts like energy and energy refills that grow more expensive the more you want to play. The actual PvP exists solely to let venerable players with multi-thousand dollar teams one shot your team while mockingly lying to you about balancing the characters. The single player aspects would be reasonably high quality for a phone game but as you can't actually play it without paying...

downloaded on a whim to get credit on a rewarded play app and haven't stopped playing for nearly 3 hours now. great visuals, interesting characters, and really fun to play. some of the game interfaces, and variety of items, can seem overwhelming but there's plenty of helpful info pop-ups to get you used to everything. 5 stars.

This game is very overwhelming. so much going on all at once. I'd say if I was a fan of Warhammer 40k, I would give it a 5 stars, I'm not really a fan. I installed for sponsorships from another company. The game itself is fantastic, has story. characters, easy to grind, and zero ads. love that. I'm sure fans of 40k Warhammer love that too. My only suggestion is a guide at the beginning of installing asking if the user is familiar with 40k or not for a tutorial of some kind.

BEST Warhammer game I've played to this date! I played back in the day a lot and this really takes me back. The units and heroes are all the same as the boardgame. its a slow grinding game with an awesome and patient community to guide you through it all. highly recommend the game, ignore all the people that complain about being ftp... thats damn near every game out there now. download and have fun!

This was a great game at the start. Now its an ad closing simulator. When you open it up you will spend the first 2 mins closing ads just to play. Then it turns into the most annoying grind ever. Honestly I love 40k and this game at launch was awesome. Now its garbage like most games on playstore. Just looking to make money not fun.

It's near impossible to get any characters you specifically want and even if you get one I guarantee it won't be one you want or were hoping for. To unlock some you have to unlock others and to unlock them others and specific campaigns so you'll never get any. But of course some especially just some you can buy them for a grueling price of $30. It's a ridiculous repetitious cash grab of an app

what a game I'm new to Warhammer but this game really makes it easy to understand what factions there are and what they do, it's like the beginners guide to this universe. It's nice to play because you don't need that much brain power to make decisions that could make you either win or lose. overall a good game to play if you're new to Warhammer

love it.. good all round. PvP, solo campaigns and events regularly. kinda slow to build up teams but you need that time to upgrade. it doesn't force you to be a pay 2 play either, but the odd event pass does help on the upgrades and roster

Best WH 40k game around imo. Truly tactical in real time and other modes. Nice graphics and user friendly layout. No pay wall or any necessity to spend money but ofcourse if you do progress is sped up. Only complaint would be a slight slow down when the combat is particularly busy. That said - a solid 4.7 stars.

Some of the parts of the game doesn't not make sense because you should have the full tutorial first. But then it skips parts of the levels to number 6 so I reckon you should have a full tutorial first separately, and then it goes on to the first level. how are you supposed to level up your characters? If you can't even get them past the certain levels. because aren't you supposed to have your character at level one and start at level 1 this is the reason why for my rating

Here is what you will deal with in this game. Want a character? Cool you need a bunch of shards to make one, which you get randomly from rmt packs. Then you need more to increase the rarity of the character. Then you need to level them up which is different then rarity. Then you need to gear them. Gear also needs to be leveled up, and have its rarity increased. Then you need to level their abilities up individually. I wish I had more than 500 characters to write a more in depth review.

Used to be a fun game that didn't have pay to win, but that's all gone now. New units are incredibly unbalanced every time a new one is released, which at first I thought was a mistake but now I realize it's deliberate to get people to spend money. I've been playing this for 3 or 4 years (or more) consistently every day, but there are people who started years after me who have armies I can't even try to match because they sunk in thousands of dollars while I'm stuck with outdated ones. I'm done.

After 6 months of gameplay, I have to say, it is still very grindy but it's more manageable now with updates like the onslaught rework. As a 40k fan, I think it's a great way to kill time, and it really rewards people who are good at long-term planning. Also, their community managers are good at engaging with their playerbase, and their customer support team is genuinely one of the best. They are some of the biggest reasons why I had stuck around & I hope they are well-paid for the work they do.

great game. i really collecting all the characters, upgrading them, sometimes little bored grinding mission but it necessary if you want free to play game. if you want a shortcut then you just buy blackstones. but i warn you, it will cost you. hahaha. happy grinding.

I've been playing this game a few days and so far it's great! I have yet to encounter any pay to win situation at all. The graphics are great, the game play is straight forward, and best of all, NO ADS!!! I'm by no means a hard-core Warhammer gamer, but love the lore and find this game to be an utter gem. Great job on this one guys, thank you!

Tacticus is fun for 40k fans and new comers alike. It's a fun turn-based stategy game that covers several armies and chapters. The gatcha mechanic is middle of the road, not generous in drop quality or amount of pulls. Just enough to entice you to spend. Energy wall limits play significantly, that's just par for the course with these types of games. All things equal, I recommend this game for any fan of turn-based strategy. 4 stars for doing the first legion dirty. Unreal.

Good game, as a newbie to WH40K I am enjoying it... but the energy refresh is ridiculous. 5 miss to replenish one energy unit an you get only one partial replenish per day by watching an ad. That is ridiculous, either shorten the refresh timer to about 3 min or give us the option to watch more ads. Til then 3 stars for what could be a 5

I haven't played this game for 828 days after having been early to install and diligent at launch. I left because of the absolutely barbaric grind to get to lv 15 even with a single champion/unit. That all said –Day 829 marks my return to the Navis Imperialis and the Emperor's embrace. It looks like the dev took the player feedback seriously. Balancing is better, the combat flows more comfortably, and the ads pushing pack purchases still aren't a main focus. I love what they're doing again <3

Relatively free-to-play friendly, fun gameplay, guild based modes are a blast, campaigns are neat and provide a good starting point, balance can be meh imo but most characters have their uses even if niche. Had to take 2 stars off though because if you leave the app (or are forced off of it by your phone alarm app) you basically run a 50/50 chance of the game not remembering you were doing something and eating your stamina or event token or whatever without giving any rewards or mission progress

I have been diving into the lore for a long time now and I don't have a pc so most 40k games are out of reach for me and I am glad that there is one for mobile that is so well put together and isn't just a pay to win you can actually grind and get the stuff you want you don't have to spend $200 just to get the stuff to beat a mission which makes this one of my favorite mobile games by default although I wish you would add Brother Sa'kan

The game is extremely pushy, pay to play, doesn't grant any longevity to a match, serious issues with collecting units, it's just another games workshop trying to grind off someone's fantasy. honestly there's much I wish was different but I understand dawn of war is the real MVP

I'm just getting into Warhammer, and when I saw this game I decided to give it a try, and boy this game is great! I love all of the characters you can unlock, and the campaigns are really cool. I'm glad to have installed this game! Also no ads! LETS GOO! WAAAGH

I like the game it doesn't make you spend real money to be able to progress its got some good strategy and the characters play very well and it's got tons of content and big names in the universe some events are annoying and it takes time to unlock characters but it's well worth sticking with it and again YOU DONT HAVE TO PAY TO WIN everything can be gotten for free with enough time bit you can buy stuff if you want

sadly, as with many mobile games, around 50% of this is 'clicking on stuff' in the menu. to open loot crates, claim quest rewards, level up characters etc. none of this adds anything meaningful to the gameplay, which is of limited complexity (at least at the start)

this is my first experience with any form of Warhammer and it's a great one no ads addictive gameplay loop cool characters I do wish they didn't shove things for you to buy with real money in your face as much but it's easy to get the hang and just a good introduction to any form of Warhammer in my opinion iv now thought about getting real Warhammer figures to try out the real game

great game... but... idk if enough characters come out fast enough? I played this years ago like 10 years ago... for a few weeks. I just came back. and I cant really say there that much more people to play with. I love the gray knights and they still ain't in the game yet?.... theres so limited chapters and characters. I just spent 100 bucks. and im disappointed bc now I see how few people there are. I dont think ill play long.

I really like these kinds of games where you can just tap to attack and it's still fun. There are many characters in the game to fight with and many battle brothers to fight alongside, but I do wish there were more free campaigns to play after the first one :)

honestly one of the few mobile games that doesnt go out of its way to p be predatory or try to force cash out of you and as such I might actually be willing to buy some of the stuff they got. it is fun and plays in a small scale turn-based strategy style which is actually pretty nice.

absolute worst experience in the world. whoever decided 1 level should be the difference between taking no damage and getting one shot should be fired and replaced by someone who actually understands level progression. biggest waste of my time.

Great game, but the updated drop rates mean you'll spend your whole life grinding tokens to upgrade ONE hero,let alone the dozens of heros in the game. Ridiculous monotonous time sink to upgrade heros

There is no world chat or direct chat. makes it impossible to talk to someone outside your clan, please fix this. tactical, well done. fairly easy to progress. this isn't that important, but they have these "guides" by goobers that are useless and annoying. get rid of that. otherwise good
it's doesn't always work as it supposed to. why Incitus save someone next to him once and in next round on the same place doesn't save at all. Great game but has these kind of bugs.
There is an 882meg required download after the tutorial section. I'm not downloading that. one star for wasting my time
no ads? perfect. jumped right into game play. no extra downloads

Awesome game for a short while. The game itself is great, including the mechanics, graphics, character upgrades, theme. However, after a few weeks it's almost unplayable as a free game and becomes a serious grind, to the point of not being playable anymore (unless you pay for insanely overpriced dlc). Agree with the other reviews, match making is also broken (not even close to being fair). The pay-to-play features really killed the game.

Have been having a good time with Tacticus over the past few weeks. Full stars because of the prompt and super helpful customer service I received on an issue that was, honestly, entirely my own doing. No back and forth, Snowprint corrected it for me and made my experience that much better. As for the game itself, I constantly have things to do in various game loops. Plenty of action and choices to make.

The gameplay isn't challenging at all. Although somewhat fun, this is a glorified slot machine. There are many in-game currencies and random "upgrades" for no reason. The game will make you tap for every single meaningless reward and at any given time you're going to have dozens of notifications to collect them. I've played it for a while and have won all battles without ever losing a single unit, there is no tactics, just an endless loop of reward collection.

Brought my review down to a 1. This game was amazing. I started playing it a few months after release in 2022. I was obsessed. I even spent money, which I have rarely done in my life on a mobile game. I spent the money because it was worth it. But after a while, the punch I purchased didn't hit hard anymore. The more updates that came, the more money and time you needed to spend for an equivalent rewarding experience. I've been off the game for 4 or 5 months now. Time better spend elsewhere.

Pretty great turn based strategy game, also a pretty great Warhammer 40k game. Has a wide variety of characters, storyline, and campaign content to play, and a rewarding return mechanic to keep you coming back each day to get a few quests done without being overly grindy. Unfortunately, it's intentionally grindy and everything about the payment mechanics are specifically designed to extract the maximum amount of money as is possible. Progression slowly grinds to a slog unless you spend $$$.

From what I've been told by people who play the tabletop, it's pretty faithful to the game. There are some obviously notable flaws though. Such as how expensive to in app purchases are, and the lack of no battle options for people that want to custom paint their own models. As well as no alternative methods for earning new units, without paying for resources, as well as a gacha mechanic that feels like it cheats you with some of the drop rates, that it burnt me out for a week.

I started this game at launch and I greatly enjoyed it. 3 and a half years later I deleted it, something I should have done a long time ago. After you beat the campaigns, if you can even get the characters to play said campaign, all that is left is farming materials just so you can try and participate in a week long event that most likely won't yield anything for you unless you invest $10 to $30 into it. You could buy an actual 40k army with the money they expect you to drop in app purchases.

There is plenty of content as one would expect for a relatively new game. However, the IAPs are insanely expensive, the lootbox mechanics are by far the worst and most predatory of any gotcha game I have seen yet. Plus, the game requires tons of grinding that is heavily time gated, and the energy refreshes to continue grinding goes up exponentially with every purchase. Yeah, it's technically "f2p", but only for about 10 minutes a day. After that, be prepared to hand over your wallet.

The gameplay is fast and good, each unit has very distinctive abilities that are interesting to learn how to use optimally. However the game requires WAY too much grinding, even for a mobile game. All the ads you see promise you many units to unlock, however unless you pay a 20+€ pack to unlock it (and you can't try it out before), it would take months to unlock it. Even doing the regular campaign doesn't reward you enough to upgrade the few units you do have, and so you have to grind even more

Its a decent free to play experience, although I feel some of the prices for a digital product are rather expensive. As others have mentioned here the game starts out relatively accessible until you hit the point where it may require you to pay for resources if you arent progressing fast enough. Also, as of late, I have noted a glitch during the guild raids where you are about to finish a fight with the boss, and the game crashes you out.

There's a great game somewhere in here, but it's drowning in clutter, microtransactions and grind. You're gonna have fun for a couple hours, then you'll hit a hard paywall. At that point, 99% of players will give up and 1% will pull out their wallets to buy imaginary currency and ultimately validate this kind of F2P model. I'm just bummed I can't play a good 40k game. Let me pay $10 and just have fun with strategy. Don't waste your time.

Updated Review (again): After thinking on it for a while, i now see why they changed it from 10 to 40. It makes pulling common characters from req drops much less frustrating and a lot more manageable. I'm still salty about being 2 shards away from gibbascrapz though, now i gotta GRIND a lot to get him. The game is still amazingly fun and a great time waster, but there are some aspects that do need changing. All in all, its an amazing game with tons of cool stuff, i just wish it had zoom.

Game is broken. A few steps into the tutorial, you're told you unlock missions, which forces you to click missions. It makes you click "claim" but you're unable to, because the tutorial still hasn't let you get enough materials to levels your characters. If you're starting new, it's literally unplayable after 3 minutes due to the glitch. I have an existing account that I can't even get to because it forces you to replay the tutorial, which is locked due to the big k mentioned.

Really fun game for the first few days, then the grind starts. The missions have clear "blocking levels" where no amount of skills will make you get through it. 10 easy level and one very hard one no graduate increase. Add MTX and agressive adds, and you start getting a better picture! It does walk the fine line between P2W and grind2W as both are possible unless you have a real life ;)

Game is great, but this game is probably the most predatory game I've ever played. The game bombards you with hundreds of dollars in "limited time:one time deals". Also, I've been getting many obnoxious bugs, such as offering me an item in the shop for Blackstone, and saying it's an upgrade even though it isn't for multiple reasons. Also, twice today, I've gone to give the last item needed to increase rank, the item is consumed, I click increase rank, it fails, and another is needed. 😡

Underwhelming would be the nice way to put it. It's ridiculously expensive to try and advance because everything you need will cost you money or a enormous amount of time. The maps are poor at best, specifically designed to force certain kinds of play. Now, they're adding "artillery", so, unless you can get one, your completely outmatched. Unless you're willing to spend money like you're playing the real warhammer 40k, don't expect to get very far.

Starts strong and quickly falls off. When you start you get great units. Gameplay is absolutely amazing and insanely addictive and fun. Eventually however you are going to slow down. And once you do this is where problems start. In order to advance your units you need more items, tokens, equipment. In order to obtain what you need you have to auto clear levels. However that's exactly when you run out of raid tokens. And that's when game becomes horrible and boring. And I actually spent money...

The game play is nice, cool characters. But two big drawbacks. You go through energy in 1 min trying to get up grades. Then you have to wait forever to get it back. 2nd some items are impossible to find. Every single person in your guild is asking for the same items. And if they don't fix those soon, it will be another deleted game forever forgot.

I absolutely love the game. It's got a great gameplay loop, frequent rewards, and lots of goals to work on. The cash store mainly serves as a way to accelerate progress or to extend play time daily. My only complaint is that after about 30-60 minutes I've exhausted all of my energy and tokens, so then I just can't play anymore. I wish there was at least one game mode that wasn't locked behind time gated regenerating resources. Doesn't even have to be that rewarding, I just want to play more.

A really fun game, and you can have a lot of fun for free. I'd have given 4-5 stars, but they keep making the monetization more and more prominent. I'm willing to support a game that's fun. I've been buying the battle pass, but now that's not enough? Now they go ahead and introduce a SUPER DUPER EXTRA BATTLE PASS while slowly decreasing the rewards from the normal battle pass and free activities. Yet another game slowly succumbing to scummy mobile tactics.

It's a fun tactics game once you have a full team but because of the gacha aspect, it falls apart fairly quickly. You hit a wall of progression and the game pushes you to spend money in order to progress, for new characters, campaigns, or battle passes. The monetization is in your face; as soon as you log in, you get hit with a banner for multiple micro transactions. It's fine if you have the time, or have money to burn. It's got some connection issues that never really get resolved, just hope.

The game has a reasonably high production value. It looks and plays nice. The positives end there, however. Much like other gacha games, the appeal quickly fades as you need to grind. The item system, energy system, the token system, and daily caps on each individual battle greatly slow down progress unless you dump a lot of cash into the game. Not worth F2P, not worth putting in $10. Designed to extract as much money as possible.

Want to have $20 packs thrown in your face every time you do something? This is the game for you. The sheer amount of micro transactions that aren't even cheap makes this a 1/5. Campaign additions are like $30 each, for a mobile game! You can spend so much money and still only get shards of a character, the $10 battle pass doesn't even give you enough character shards to unlock the featured character!

Every one of these "gacha" style games has a wall where progress becomes VERY slow if you don't pay money. I tend to rate games by how long it takes to get there and this is one of the worst ones by that standard. Just a few hours in and WELL before you finish the 'normal' campaign the enemies become hard enough that strategy means nothing and all that's left is slowly accumulating upgrades with the tiny "energy reserves" you accrue. There's no "gitgud" just an incremental slog.

Can't play anymore. It's a pretty fun game with lots of things to do at first. However, it uses an energy system that takes 30mins to generate enough for 1 attempt at a 30s mission. So you quickly end up only being able to play about 5-10min per day. Refill purchases are extremely pricy and not a practical option IMO. Would rate much higher if I could play more.

Previous me was a fool. The greed gets worse and worse. $28 for an event and you don't even get a character from it. Game wants you to spend money but money doesn't even help you advance at all season pass - can't even get half way up it as everything in the game is time locked. You can play an hour at a time that's it. Dont get this game. Literally any other gotcha game would be better. Past- Just started but can see how it's fun but maybe a little heavy on selling stuff right off the bat.

I really want to like this game. mobile version of kill team with the ability to build lists like the tabletop? sounds great! but I cant shake the feeling of having my time wasted. first of all any game with an energy mechanic doesn't want you to play it, it wants to become a habit by forcing you to check in every so often. second, in my experience so far tactics aren't as important as character power levels. it may be possible to have fun here but you'll need to fight through the monitization.

Fun to play at first (like through the first 2 bosses), but the levels just get pointlessly hard to play after a while, trying to get you to pay to progress. It also locks you into using the weakest and most worthless characters throughout mkst missions, so even if you do pay for better characters, you can't use them. Can't say I would recommend.

This is a fun game. However, the monetization aspect is overdone, and you can't play if you're out of energy and tokens. A better monetization model could make this a better game. Perhaps monetize by allowing character customization and maybe a small monthly fee ($5) to play. The reason for the one-star review is that I find the game to be a tedious, redundant grind, which quickly becomes boring. I had to uninstall.

This game is fun, but 6 plus minutes for one energy vial is insane. I want to play more but I'm not going to spend a bunch of shards on energy when I'd rather roll the reqs. That's another issue, it's pretty gambly. There's no way to progress on getting characters you want, except for praying for a random drop. Also missions, such as Thaddeus Noble's missions, pretty much any you unlock by beating the boss stage, are stopped in its tracks if you don't have it. I'd love to see combination of toke

I don't often write reviews like this, but I'm enjoying the game so I thought I'd give opinions to make it better. However I've only been playing a few days so my opinion may change. First, I like how the combat feels, it moves quickly and the mechanics are at least loosely related to the tabletop. The art is solid, and the characters feel like genuine GW. Suggestions: Improve the acquisition rate of requisition drop orders (slightly) and continue to add more factions to the game.

It starts off fun as you progress through a campaign but then becomes a mind-numbing slog as you have to grind out levels, stars, and gear to advance any further. Also, there's a limit to how much you can grind a stage for items, with a 24-hour cooldown. There's not really enough tactics in the battles, and it's definitely a pay to win gacha game.

Ok, had a couple of days to play this. I set my review at 2 stars. The polish on the game looks great. The game itself, like final fantasy tactics is refreshing. That's where the positives end. After a day or two of playing (less than that if you're retired like me), you will quickly run out of the various tokens/tickets you need to play. You never seem to know how many tokens you have, but it's never enough. Pay to win, without a doubt.

Progression is a snails pace and the game makes it quite difficult to unlock. I'm not looking to no life a gacha game that only allows me to play an hour a day to hamstring my progress. The prices in the shop are also insane and outright lie about sales (80% off this bundle when the price dropped from $29.99 to $19.99). Gameplay isn't well explained and certain features and mechanics are never mentioned leading to some irritating "gotcha" moments (just like the tabletop I suppose). Not a fan

Update! I downloaded this game again to give it a chance because I love 40k. It's still terrible. The offer prices are the highest I have ever seen. Basically, it's a gotcha game but without the fun gameplay or graphics or genshin impact and the like. Unlocking and leveling new characters takes literally months. Only try if you love repetitive grinding. The absolute dragging of the 40k license through the mud is heartbreaking. This is not worth your time. I wanted to like it but it is not good.

Great game, but the grind is long and tiring. The fact that you can save up 10 requisitions, which supposedly earns you a new character, and still rarely get a new character, is infuriating. I spend all this time saving requisitions because it says you'll get a new character and you don't. Most often you just get some shards for a character you already have. It's useful, sure. But it's not a new character, they just want to keep you grinding. The truth hides in the small print. Disappointed af.

Game was really fun and I was enjoying my time playing it, but from the first minute it's clear that this game has a huge focus on micro (macro?) transactions, and you'll quite quickly get to a point where you need to start buying packs if you want to complete the legendary release events / bigger challenges to unlock characters. The game and gameplay itself? Easy 5/5, amazing. But buyer beware, you'll quickly reach the point where buying expensive packs are mandatory to complete events.

It's whatever , I've seen the same mechanics done over and over again. Plays like every other game of its type tbh. Abilities are meh. Everything cost energy to get you to spend. You hit a wall very fast in the beginning where you can't progress in the campaign because you're too weak. Resources are scarce and the places you get them are locked behind limited energy events. Just another pointless , lazy , boring grind if you want to get anywhere in this game.

The game play and events are great. But this game is greatly held back by the cool downs of everything. I'm lucky to play for more than 20min a day because of cool downs. Especially when you hit the leveling wall, forces you to either spend money or wait for hours/days just to do anything else. I'll give this 5 stars if they ever lower the cooldown times. It's ridiculous.

This game has the POTENTIAL to be good. But is super scummy with it's asking prices for just about everything. $30 for a new campaign? Are you freaking serious? And the discount prices listed are lies! At least it's not filled with ads so that's something I guess. Like most mobile games you will hit a wall where progression grinds to halt and without dropping serious cash, good luck getting anywhere. There are also far too many currencies. For a newcomer it is INCREDIBLY confusing starting out.

Fun at the start, huge grind incoming or else pay to win. This plays a lot like an extremely simplified version of PC Warhammer games. The early missions cover the basics well. The ads for micro transactions come fast and early. As you complete campaign missions you will begin to hit arbitrary skill walls. Early in the game these are simple to overcome, just play a different mini game until you level/gear up some. The paywall comes at you hard near mission 50 or ranked arena. Pay4win game.

I think the progression curve is broken. Starts out too easy and quickly gets impossible. You can't get the characters you want. I've been playing for a couple weeks and still haven't gotten a single tau character. Really wish it was a better game, because the actual tactics and battling are pretty fun. But, by the time I get an army I want, the characters I don't like will be so powerful that new characters won't be able to keep up.

You'll have a little fun as it's a nice little tactical strategy game. But as gatcha games go, this one puts a slowdown to your progress very early. Typical free to play incentives but I don't think you can expect to play many of the modes without shelling out some real money, or by planning on sitting around for the months it would take to unlock enough characters. I don't even see progress easily made by spending a modest amount. It's either Moby dick style spending or nothing.

Money grab!!!! Play for a little while but the difficulty exponentially climbs half way through the free campaign. Using the 10 requisition drop gives you a guaranteed character but gives you characters you already have and doesn't help you in the campaign you're in. You can pay $30 for each new campaign! It drives you to spend money in the worst way. Not worth the time or money. There are better games in the store for free or much less money.

The game has the potential to be a fun mobile game but it's hampered by a ridiculous spike in difficulty that requires you play a very specific way or by dumping a bunch of money, which the developers don't hide with how many "special deals" they shove in your face endlessly. It was fun for the first few hours but I'd rather not spend my free time grinding for in game currency. I'm sure there's fans willing to pay that price though.

It's very hard to figure out what's going on? I can fight in one game, pvp, but then all of sudden, the next game im out ranked 3-5×'s better. The upgrades are endless and only get harder to find parts to upgrade, and the upgrades are very confusing as to what you actually upgraded. There are so many things going on, so many things it wants u to download as well. The game is too much for mobile memory, and the time it takes to accomplish anything is ridiculous.

I want to like this - I really do. But the various currencies used to power up trickle in unless you dump dollars on loot boxes. There are plenty of game modes, but most of them are on a 3/day cool down. Unlocking characters can take over a hundred shards, but you only get 1 at a time. Buying characters is also ver steep (bundles for almost $50). If you're okay with grinding at a tenth of a snail's pace - you'll love it. Otherwise give it a miss.

The gameplay itself is fun as hell. If this was just rating the game, it's an easy 5/5. That being said: it does have a variety of limited resources that will likely have the player hit a hard progression wall at one point (likely right about the time you get addicted). Timers will resupply some of them, but not all. For a FTP game, that's par for the course. They need to make money somehow, and I respect it. I'm also cheap, though, so I'm docking a point for preying on my gaming addictions

The game is good. The graphics are decent. You teach people how to play the game unlike many other supposed game/trap makers. I don't have an issue with cash, I haven't spent a cent and have an okay lineup. I would cash support but the issue is the other characters I can't build up because I have to play with one faction when I want to play split factions off the bat. It's mind numbing putting work into common characters when you have an Epic not able to get gear because you can't level it.

Personally, I absolutely love this game, the levels aren't too hard and I've been itching to play more Warhammer games. This game is way more fun than I thought it would be. I thought that it would be PvP based but it's actually PvE. I've been having a hard time finding a decent PvE to put my time into but this game fixed that. If you're still not sure if you'd like the game, just play the first 5-15 missions or so, they aren't long so it won't take up too much of your time.

Having now played for a few months, I gotta drop my score to 3. The gameplay is solid and there is a good amount of stuff to do everyday, but the drop rate for characters is ABYSSMAL. That's a problem when big chunks of content are only playable once specific characters are available. Events are designed around players with deep, high-level rosters, but there's kind of no way to get those or level them. Play till you're bored, but don't spend money. It won't get you much anyway.

This isn't a game. It's a scam. It's designed to be impossible. Don't waste your time on it. It will always move units in the dumbest places. It will randomly rearrange your unit setup. Enemies will get crits far more frequently than you will, no matter what items you select. It will keep giving you intrusive pop-ups to trick you into using this game's specialty resource out of frustration. The only way to fully complete stages is by spending real money to upgrade your characters to max.

So the combat is a lot of fun, I enjoy it a lot. But my god, this is the grindiest mobile game I have ever played - and I have played a lot. The rewards from every activity is so stingy - sometime 1-2 premium currency (you need 300 for a single summon). Energy is extremely hard to come by and you have to spend it on stages to unlock new heroes and empower your existing ones. It can take maybe 4-5 days to upgrade one of the 6 gear slots. Theres a fun game here, but it is only hurting itself.

Really fun for the first two chapters. Has the bones to be a great game. The paywall is painfully obvious by the third chapter, as my stronger characters get one shotted constantly, leading to be unable to farm materials. If character progression and collection wasn't so brutal, and with how little you get for your money in the cash shop, this would have easily been one of the best WH40K mobile games.

Good visuals. Fun when you can play. Hard pay walls. Multiple season passes, Unlocking characters is effectively meaningless as you can't play campaigns without a group of 5 for that faction. Everything, and I mean everything, is priced through the roof. Games better than this entire cash grab are less than one character. $30 so you can unlock one campaign that can not be finished. There is no way to make slow, steady, consistent progress. Skip until it becomes an actual game.

Pay to progress (and it's expensive). The gameplay itself is fun. But it quickly turns into a boring slog to unlock more characters. And buying anything in the store is ludicrously expensive. There is not even a way to just pay to unlock the characters in the faction you want to play. You have to buy stupid loot boxes that will MAYBE get you a character you want.

Really like the game play, but extremely grindy and slow to progress. Paying money really doesn't speed things up much either. I dont mind spending a few dollars on games I like, but some of the stuff in here is just silly. Was offered to pay $15.99 to buy 45 shards of a character. Even if I wanted to pay that, you need 130 shards to unlock them. It is crazy to have an option to pay that much and not actually unlock the character to use.

I'm torn between how much I love this game and its IP, and how predatory its monetization strategies are. A character I am fond of just wrapped a time-limited event. She is no longer available, save at random. I spent $90 ($30 three times) to enhance my ability to access her. I came as close as one can (140/150 points) but the event favored to more dedicated players (whales). Lo and behold, there's a 24-hour-only, $30 offer available to finish the quest. I didn't get what I paid a lot for.

it's fun, but there are way too many currencies to manage, some of which can't even be bought. the MTX are also extremely overpriced. the battlepass for this game costs more than actual triple A experiences battlepasses, and they will sell you mini passes to speed up event progress along side battlepasses and random pull supply drops. if you aren't willing to spend money, I would skip it all together. It also has an energy system on top of extremely grindy mechanics.

Initial gameplay is quite good. However, after reaching a certain point (about 5 days of gameplay for me) you CANNOT progress any longer without spending money. I have played pvp, and every pve segment available. My characters still do not have the required materials to level up and can't compete in battles at this stage in the game without getting one shotted. Upgrades were made, resources were grinded, there is no physical way to progress on my account at this point.

Enjoyable but ridiculously grindy and has a very limited amount of time to play. Like a certain star wars game, it focuses too much on grinding out gear to level up characters. Though there is a strategy gameplay and the factions are cool, it limits you to play ultramarines most of the time. The events are have very poor rewards. The game makes and forces you to pay money mostly. There is not really a lot to achieve in this game to be honest. Far to grindy. And I'm very disappointed.

Good, with room for improvement. The game is fun and has a lot of good modes to play, but the amount of time it takes to get energy, onslaught attempts, and salvage run attempts is way too long. The character upgrades require you to use an insane amount of energy so it could take you days to get a single upgrade, even at low levels. This makes it difficult to get stronger to beat campaign missions. Like most mobile games, this is pay to win.

It's SUPER p2p. Some levels are basically impossible without grinding for an hour or paying. The energy is also stupid it's in every one of these types of games, and it's so annoying with no reason to be added. U have to repeat some levels multiple times in order to upgrade once, which basically does nothing. Luckily, they added an auto play mechanic so u don't have to sit thru them. Sadly, they still use up energy, so u can only do it 15 times. (Aslo 3 characters is 30 entire dollars)

This game is so p2w it's actually sickening. There's an energy system, there's a ticket system for raiding levels, there's an absurd amount of grinding for materials, levels, and star ranks. And don't even dream of getting a new character with pulls, you'll get your feelings hurt. All of these (premium currency, energy, materials, etc.) culminate into only about 20 min of play a day unless you spend money. If you want a f2p game that isn't riddled with microtransactions, this ain't it.

The game itself is pretty fun, but holy moly the monetization is predatory. In most games you can at least justify buying a battle pass because once you have it you have it they typically contain enough things to buy the next battle pass without spending any more money as long as you make it far enough in, not in this game. You have to buy each battle pass separately, and the prices are very high relative to what you get. At the end of the day it's a gacha game.

Definitely skip. As others mentioned, there's a good game in here, but you'll never get to play it because the monetization is almost satirical. Every little thing has a fee attached to it and everything has a wait timer attached to it. The game is very stingy with anything free, but it also looks like $100 wouldn't get me very far either. There's an ad for this or that bundle on every other screen and even pop-ups for IAPs that'll sometimes not let you close them. Real tired of gacha shards.

A decent turn based tactical game with some interesting mechanics. But, as many pay to win/play, to many resources, to many events and specials offers, to many cluttering menu's, and a simply confusing upgrade and equipment system. So much clutter... I like the game, i don't like the typical 'free' android game amount of confusion and horrendous menu's. I couldn't even find how the play the actual game at first, but could easily find mountains of bundels for enormous amount of money.

Shame on me for thinking this game would be worth anything. Paid to get requisitions, thinking I could requisition from a faction I actually want to play, and it's just a garbage loot crate system, got a common of what I want to play and an epic for one I don't. Wish I could get my money back, what an absolute waste of time. Games workshop strikes my wallet and my hopes again. Do yourself a favor and don't even bother. I'm done after an hour and a half of playing.

In terms of graphics, animation, and play style, it's amazing. And it reminds me of playing table top again. Buuuuut, it is licensed by GW.. and with that comes a hefty price on something that you don't get very much for. yes, you can grind and not pay a dime, but how many years do you have. and when you do spend money, say on the battle pass.. well, prepare to waste a lot of time on a grind that is clearly just a money grab. the time it would take to complete it is unrealistic, and unfair.

Fun tactical game, do keep in mind that this game is trying to get you to spend money for campaigns, characters, and upgrades. So if you're looking for a game to play for free and trying to earn your rewards, this game is not it. However, if you don't mind eventually buying more content, you'll be in for a treat. Just wish they allow people to still enjoy the story at the expense of leveling up characters (Like trying before you buy).

I have been playing the game for almost a year. The game mechanics are nice. The economic incentives are very greedy. There is no loyalty on behalf of the game developers towards the players. Parts of the game are eternally in the "coming soon" fase. It's basically a casino camouflaged as a fremium, every time you spend money you don't know what you to get, and the chance to advance in the game gets more riskier with less certainties for advancement.

I feel gridlocked in my gameplay experience. I feel like I'm being forced to purchase characters. It's fine. I get it, but it's losing 2 stars from me. May lose more as time goes on if gridlocking players is the way it is. Was very enjoyable at first, though, so don't get me wrong. Really don't like how the gaming industry gridlocks players, especially with certain games. I would rather pay a base price and be able to legitimately enjoy Warhammer for all its worth.

Wanted to wait until I hit the pay wall before rating. Which seems to be right around campaign level 50. From that point in if you really want to get anywhere you're going to have to spend. And seeing as how paying for "supply drops" means you'll guaranteed get a single character every 10 summons. You're going to be stuck here for WAY longer than this game is worth. It's fun, just not worth the money to "git gud" don't waste your time, it's just like every other phone game. They all suck.

New pop-up ads make me want to uninstall and never look back. I've been playing for a couple of years and spent some money, but now there are pop-up ads in the most recent update that makes me want to uninstall the game. Edit for the dev reply: these are forced pop-up ads OVER the game. I'm fine with clicking on "watch ad" for a reward. But these are forced over the gameplay where I have to "x" out of it.

Well paced at first, but becomes a crawl way too quickly. Some characters require 150+ tokens to unlock or rank up, so getting them 1 at a time is frustrating. Each boss let's you get a 33% chance at a token 7 times a day. Even the uncommon characters push 70+ tokens. Then the gear system, which is itself Hella grindy. Skill tokens come so short, and a single overpowered character skill can make or break a fight. The massive upgrade cost is just a major wall for free to play.

While this is one of the more enjoyable warhammer games, I have to say that the prices are not very very very cheap, It also lacks voice acting which is ashamed, it would have been nice to have some hammy lines, wa rcrys and so on like Dawn of War's voices. Animation are simple and the art style is pretty uh unique... You'll get used to it. Gameplay is actually fun and engaging and requires the use of your brain which is a plus. Gacha rates aint bad too, Pretty okish. Recommend.

after you beat the first few campaigns the game becomes incredibly grindy. every upgrade for your characters can take weeks to complete. black stone (the premium currency) gets you very little. the difficulty of the Legendary events that have all of the cool characters climbs super fast. Honestly, I really enjoyed this game until I just hit this wall. it would be nice if they added new campaigns to play, but we only get new characters.

This isn't a game so much as it is a pervasive attempt to sell you power and resources at every conceivable opportunity. Unlock a new character? They want to sell you the levels. New event? They want you to shell out money so you can skip it. New campaign? They want to sell you every character they released for 49.99. This is just marketing with a very thin layer of Warhammer. Save your sanity and your wallet and just go do something else. This ad campaign is not one you should support.

This really is a slow grind game. If you're looking for game that you can play for hours a day and make good progression then this is not the for you. The refresh resource rate is painfully slow and the character unlock system is truly excruciating! Its good that it seems to be free to unlock everything . But the time is going to take to do that just doesn't seem worth it!

It's an "okay" game, but it's so bogged down by the myriads of ways that it wants you to spend money and unlock things that it quickly becomes overwhelming. There are 3 types of currency, individual characters' tokens for unlocking or upgrading over 100 characters, $30 "campaign packs", multiple types of loot crates, missions, and all of this vying for your attention all on the main screen. It's less of a game and more of a confusing visual cocophany hoping to trick you into spending money.

It's an excellent game. Lots of thought had gone into the mechanics and character details. However like all freemium games you hit the grind near the end of the first campaign. You have a choice; you can start giving away your money (and it's not cheap) or uninstall. I uninstalled, and I recommend you do the same. Games that play on people's addictions to take thier money is akin to a gambling habit. The loot system with chests and random items are the same mechanics. Don't fall for it.

One of the greediest games on the Play store. I gave the real money up front, but realized really quick, you think your getting a good character for real money, but it is really a bare bones character! They really give you nothing for real money! Very sad, I had high hopes for what I thought was a real game, but instead got one of the worst monetizations on Play store.

Game is fun, it has really tugged at my 40k nostalgia. The rating could easily go up if the in game purchases (ie: items to progress your characters / weapons / play more levels in a day) were not so exorbitant. I don't mind shilling some cash at a game, I understand I am getting a (far from) "free" game, but this is nuts.

I was playing the game completely free, and I got about a 1/3 of the roster with access to all the default campaigns and I was close to getting the alternative ones with time. The devs updated the game with the new guild stuff which was interesting for a bit, but then I noticed they raised the unlock requirements massively on all characters. They also removed daily quests which were the only feasible way to earn the resources to get characters. They slowed the game down so you spend more. Sucks.

Pretty fun game. Edited: This game let's you start off pretty fun but you're quickly held off if you don't spend money. The only way to "rank up" is upgrading your characters and the best way to do that is spend real life money on the game. Grinding without money basically eventually brings you to a stagnant point where every enemy is insanely overpowered compared to your characters and your progress is haunted to "daily free drops" that give you nothing to further your progress. Game is a trap

I want to love this game. It's actually managed to get warhammer mostly right and coontinues to expand its offered factions. The problem is after awhile the free rewards dry up, the campaign's run out and the same guild boss battles play out while you try to get within a certain rank level. Long story short progressing and overall just playing the game has begun to feel like a chore and I'd rather do something else. Check back in a few months to see if they've added any depth.

It's a good, thoughtful game- but it's pay to win. The garenteed character drop for 10 scrolls/ 3k gems is a straight up lie. You get character shards, not another character. Usually, when you get character shares you get ones you already have, which is terrible, because there's a bunch of levels you can't play until you have certain characters. Some levels you can mix in match within the same overall faction, others not- for no explainable reason other than they want more money. I'm all set.

The game is so slow, it takes so long to earn enough to get the 10 person gatcha so you can get the guaranteed character only for it to be one you already have. Feels like the game is pushing you to pay to progress, because only certain characters can play certain stories, and it takes so long to get any characters without paying ≈30$ which is beyond ridiculous to play a mobile game.

It's fun for the first week or two... Then you realize the cost to do missions goes up, the amount of times you have to mission to get what you need goes up, and what does it cost to do that? Money! I paid for a "character guaranteed" and I only got stuff for characters I already had. It's a scam, and the scam gets bigger the longer you play.

Thankfully I read the reviews. You shouldn't have to join a discord to find out how to progress in a game without spending money. As a game dev, I was always taught that if you have to explain everything about your game, specifically how to progress or have fun, you have failed miserably. The need to buy a new chapter RIGHT after starting the game is frankly disgusting. I'd rather pay for the app and be done with it. What this does is set the tone for the game. Get ready to pay, repeatedly.

I'm gonna start with the pros: it's fun to play (at first) and you get to see the 3D models which look wonderful. The combat is fun. Unfortunately after the intro section progression is a serious struggle without paying. When you tap something there's a solid half second delay between the tap and the menu to actually show up, so you end up tapping a few times which causes the menu to disappear. The game has potential if it made getting new characters and upgrades easier.

game play is fine. the problem is in the characters. too hard to get character shards, too hard to gear up and the requisition pulls are a joke. been playing for years now and I have only gotten 1 good one. also, the character releases are a nightmare. you either need to be on the game for hours or have the perfect setup for the events. they don't actually tell you in advance what the events will entail. they require you to accomplish certain things but you can't sort your roster by the thing.

The game is fine, there is entertainment, good models and a variety of skills and compositions to say it is a strategy game. That being said grind kills the enjoyment, the new event completely makes the Arena unplayable when the enemy has higher points, which was not a problem before. Indeed lore is missing, the campaign is somewhat nice though, could push new people into books or other media about 40K.

I like the setting a lot so I thought I'd give it a try. It is a fun tactical game. Starts very slow and easy but gets more interesting as the game continues. The progression is slow but there are a bunch of fun modes to try out. However, this is all ruined by everything having an energy cooldown. Want to play the story? Sorry out of energy. Want to fight in the arena? Not enough tokens. It is this way for every mode. Without the energy system, I might actually recommend this game.

The game is far better than I expected a Warhammer mobile game to be. Tacticus does have monetization though I find being primarily F2P ( I put 20 bucks in since I like Warhammer). It's more than fine progression. The roster of characters isn't huge but it isn't small either. Eight factions with 5 characters each. The turn based gameplay is fun and every character feels unique and lore appropriate in what their abilities do. I wish PvP tokens regen faster or hope for a casual mode for fun.
