Massive $30 pay walls just to play campaign. Campaign is probably the only aspect I find interesting in this game and only the first one is free. Part 2 and 3 are $30 each and 4 is $20. You could just buy Space Marines 2 deluxe edition for that price. Not something most people would be willing to pay on a mobile game. Consider a price adjustment in the future.

Can't proceed after just a few minutes. I was playing just the tutorial and got to where it tells me to upgrade my characters, I followed it to upgrade the first guy twice, then it says I've unlocked missions and I can't do anything but go there. It tells me to claim the reward but I've only done 2/4 upgrades and can't claim it. However, the game won't let me do anything else. So I click claim and it says "complete to claim rewards" over and over.

NOT AN OFFLINE GAME. FALSELY ADVERTISED. The game itself is great but I downloaded it because it's advertised as being an offline game, which it isn't. Not at all. Game is not an offline game, it requires full internet connection to play. If it wasn't for this I would have rated the game so much higher, the game is a great online gacha for mobile, but I went into it assuming I would be able to play it without internet, as it says "offline" and false advertisement is always inexcusable.

CONS- over monetized, tiny rewards for accomplishments, insanely stingy with in game currency, get unit shards not always a unit PROS- Good character detail, strong gameplay, good graphics, runs smooth RANT- how the hell have I beat over 70 missions and I haven't got enough currency to buy 10 units. The fun in games like these is earning a shot at the slot machine for new stronger units. The developer had no problem adding multiple in game purchases over 20 dollars. Fix this

I have to admit, it was very fun at first! Sadly this type of gameplay doesn't lend itself well to the way they set up gatcha, or how long it takes to power up units. I have to admit, as a diehard 40k fan, it was sad to see how much the story has gotten butchered. It leaked into this game, and honestly, it... it ruined the experience even more. Adios for now.

Okay game, but unsurprisingly greedy. It uses a shard system for characters instead of just giving you the full character in drops/pulls, so for some characters you can spend eternity trying to get the 500 shards you need at an agonizing pace. If they'd just let you get the characters rather than their jigsaw pieces, and didn't lock content behind having certain characters, it'd be a lot better.

Gave it a good try... I guess it's alright. It's a little boring. It's tedious like most mobile games and has a massive difficulty leap to get you spending. Uninstalled after trying all the features so I could give an honest review. Unless you're a Warhammer fan, the game itself isn't going to mean much to you. I'm not even going to say it has potential; it's just another Gacha game with Warhammer fans in mind. 2 out of 5 for chess style game play, and semi-interesting story... Don't recommend.

After playing the game for a longer period, I'm editing my original post. They need to create a wishlist of characters to increase the chances of getting heroes that will allow you to progress through the game or adjust to the current meta. I have been stuck for a while now due to summoning characters that haven't allowed me to progress past the initial imperial campaign. Very pay-to-win and not worth downloading.

Fun game to play and past the time, although there have been some issues since the most recent update, the main thing is losing most of my raid tickets which you need to farm items quickly or better yet not receiving them in the first place, they are necessary to progress in this game and if you don't receive them have fun waiting your entire day.

Terrible game. For one the in app purchases are typical GW insanely higher than they should be prices, stuff that in similar games would cost 5 is 40 but honestly no surprise there. The issue is that you hit a wall progress wise were the difficulty of enemies out scales what you get "normally" for your team, meaning you hit a point where you either can't proceed because you just get one shot by anything, or you shell out $50+ to keep playing, rinse and repeat every so often. Would not recommend

Great art with an interesting style, however it's a game that uses an energy system to play... Which kills my desire to play at all. The game loop and gameplay is dry and uninspired, there aren't nearly enough characters at launch, and the leveling system is a total grind. Prepare yourself for endless store pop-ups, shameless monetization focused gameplay, and gatcha character draws. I'm sure it's fine if I want to be dumping $200 or more into it... But I don't.

Just another manipulative cash grab mobile game. Only generous at first glance, with plentiful rewards for the first 30 levels (sounds like a lot but each level takes maybe 3 minutes). Once the normal reward structure takes over the game slows to a crawl and you get lots of prompts to buy characters for $5 or $10 each or mission packs for $30. Extremely limited gameplay, with each character having only 2 abilities and no meaningful way to switch up gameplay without tons of grinding.

Honestly, was disappointed after a couple or so days. The game is just too repetitive and is a cash grab and a half. The story is just generic and is too comparable to thousands other games like it. It doesn't offer much long term. It's fun for a couple missions. But after awhile, it wears on you and you kinda just lose intrest quickly with little to drive you to come back.

The games fun, but trying to earn orders for new characters is unbearable not considering your odds of getting a new character are poor. You can farm some characters but for like a legendary one expect to put half a year into it and that being the only mission you ever play. Literally saps the life out of the game. Its crazy grindy too for leveling characters. Really could be great game but limited by greed.

Fun game ruined by the pay wall. Prices are high relative to what you get. 10-15 bucks just to level up a couple abilities. $30+ just to unlock characters that are necessary to even PLAY the campaigns. Then you have to pay to upgrade those units to use in the campaigns since free mas are rare. Requisitions rarely give you 5 shards to unlock one of many legendary units, which require 250-500 shards. Or you can pay for in game currency to buy 3-10 shards. Very expensive just to play, save your $$$

Extremely repetitive gameplay, monetization, absolutely crammed down your throat. Every time you load a page and really, you can't advance unless you spend money and believe me, they try every way they can think of to frustrate you into spending money. It is a really fun time killer, though, just don't try to win because it's going to cost you a lot of money.

The turn based gameplay itself is pretty fun and has some interesting mechanics and characters. The paywall is absolutely brutal. You end up grinding over tiny bonuses in boring repeatable content just trying to get good enough for the end of the first campaign. I wasn't able to save up for a single 10 pull before giving up on it. The gacha game experience missed the mark by quite a bit.

Requisition drop "Guaranteed character" is not guaranteed. If you take the time to save up, a week or two, the game states you are guaranteed a character from the requisition drop. What the "Guaranteed character" actually means, is you get a character but it might be one you already have. In that case you don't get a new character. This makes the 113 characters in the game currently almost impossible to unlock.

Found this game because it was in the offline games section. It is fun, but even small things can't be done offline and it really degrades the experience to have had those expectations. Frankly, there are a lot of things that you should be able to do offline that you can't. One of those things is any campaign mission. Edit: Dropped an extra star cause now randomly it prevents me from playing occasionally because of the connectivity requirement. Even though I have internet when it stops me.

Ive been playing this game most days of the week for months. It is a very heavy grind, it is very challenging to unlock and upgrade characters. Often taking weeks just to level up one character only one level unless you are willing to spend money. They constantly try new way to make you spend money in the app. It recently started a battle pass :| which is not easy to grind Ive bearly put a dent into it and I've been playing every day from the pass launch Do not install or give them money.

The game could be a lot of fun, and is when you start - the game becomes unplayable unless you spend money rather quickly. It locks you into using certain characters, which you have to level up, that are basically useless in the grand scheme. Every bit of this game is built to play against your psychology, to get you to spend more and more money. The events they have could also be fun - but they are so heavily weighted to folk that are high level that it is literally punishing to be low level.

Still new to the game but so far it's fun enough to play. I love the graphics but there a lot going on that hasn't been explained. The game seems really busy and cluttered with almost zero explanation of what to do and why. The maps are tiny and in all honesty, for the price they want, I'd rather just spend the money on the table top game. Greedy, greedy developers. They offer so little and ask for so much.

I'm really enjoying this game. The tactics and strategy are deeper than I expected, and there's a lot of detail given in the tool tips. Has the usual array of mobile game cash grabbiness, but it's on par with other games and just the way of things now. Shockingly seems to be ad free, but I'm not very far in yet. Kudos devs if that's correct! One minor complaint for me is I think the combat animations are too fast. Makes some of the fights seem anticlimactic

Honestly if I could just buy the army I wanted I'd be cool, but instead you have deal with "requisitions" which are like tickets that you use to gamble for possible shards that's completely random. I've got like seven or eight models from four different armies, and it's just not that kinda game that I really wanna spend the amount of time necessary to unlock the models I want for end game stuff that's just there to see if they can squeeze a few extra dollars out of you.

Boring, money hungry, uninspired. That sums up the gist of the entire game. The game is extremely shallow and boring. In order to get materials to upgrade your characters, the devs ask that you pay anywhere from $30-90 upfront so that you can play missions that will have upgrade materials. The 'combat system' has no depth, and neither do the characters. Ie, if you want to play Space Marines, then have fun charging blindly into sniper fire because only 3 or 4 Marines have ranged weapons. Bad

pretty stingy with the units, outside of the default ones you get in the game you won't be getting any units for a long time. you can grind for them and get some that way but most games at least give you one free draw. the only draw they give you is a fixed unit, not really a draw at all. gameplay is decent, but there are other decent games out there.

Game is great, but you're stuck SO MUCH, by design! The campaigns (best bit if you ask me) are shut down by obscure acquirements of characters and way too slow farming, designed to make you cash-out. If you spend thousands then yeah the tempo is fine, but who got thousands for a mobile game? Farming for upgrades is sometimes impossible if the right campaign is not unlocked (or you don't pay). And the rewards usually give you shards for characters you might never want to use.. let me choose!

Game is grindy. Paid 45.00AUD for 3 characters (I wanted chaos) as a head start. It's day 3 and I've already hit walls. You can only grind a certain amount per day so in order to progress you need to powerup characters. Their is a limit per day as to how much you can grind to power them up. the game is designed about you playing it for as long as possible. I haven't even got my full team yet but im expecting it'll take months, maybe a year. One year of grind for 45.00aud. Don't reccomend

The overall game mechanism is ok, but you have to either buy stuff with real money or really patient in order to progress. Everything is very hard to get, and if you're stuck on certain level, it'll take literally days of playing to advance. All the dev cares about is money, which means no recharge, no experience.

Fairly fun, simple turn based tactics game. It has an 'energy' system set up so that you can get a good amount of gameplay in per day without paying. However, the level up ramp is so steep only a few previous levels provide any challenge, and to progress you're constantly up against a difficulty wall which you can only overcome through grinding rather than skill. The energy and rewards system is buggy as anything too, energy sometimes just evaporates and rewards sometimes just don't register.

The game leaves a lot to be desired. I don't know if it's just the first few campaigns, maybe it'll get better as I fully unlock the game. It doesn't really have the tactical aspect that you would expect from fantasy tactics, suikoden, or any other tactics base game. Honestly this would just be better as a turn-based game but. I guess my main issue or concern are the small maps that don't allow you to move around and actually do any tactics. Doesn't feel right to call it a tactics game yet.

It's a fun game. I like the gameplay, the animations, the music, upgrading troops, and collecting characters. That all being said this game is pay to win to the point of almost being unplayable. The prices aren't aweful to buy stuff but my gosh if you just want to play the campaigns and collect characters it's impossible without spending some money.

A few hours in and it basically is still a tutorial. I feel the only way I will die is if I just sit there and not attack. Graphics I actually like, the idea of gameplay seems good, but thus far I do not feel like I am really playing anything. Hitting move then attack knowing I won't lose is annoying. Maybe this game just starts slow, so I'll give another few hours. If it is good this review will change. If not, then the game has been deleted.

After a few dozens of levels that can be played for free, development of characters requires a few thousand dollars. I understand making money, or selling a game for 20-50$. But this is a neverending cash ripper. Upgrading fully one character is a 1000. There are dozens of characters that we have to have to progress. What is good about the game is that it has the spirit of Warhammer 40K. Apart from woke elements. Women astartes with heavy flamers... Yeah... We only miss the Snow White here.

Played the game for a few days now, it's great, intuitive gameplay, you need strategy and tactics to actually win, very satisfying overall. Unfortunately the energy system kills it for me, i hate waiting in order to be able to play, or pay for energy, not my thing. Also the premium currency, black stone, is so hard to get, you get miniscule amounts, and a 10× draw costs 3000 stones. I love Warhammer, both fantasy and 40k, and the game is great overall, despite what i said above, i do recommend

To be honest its a unique game and that's the only reason I'm giving it two stars. But it's pay to win or wait days to upgrade so you can win. I'd much rather play another game then wait on cool downs and a chance for upgrades to drop on this one. It honestly got to the point where I was repeating one battle over and over for two days straight, which in my opinion for a mobile game is very annoying. Lastly the dlc cost way to much. This is a mobile game so drop your prices.

Very frustrating. Everything looks great and is initially fun to play, but it doesn't take long before you're getting pounded by a horde of necron scrubs who will kill at least one of your characters per round. The items needed to level up are hidden behind paywalls or impossible to get, so you kind of hit a brick wall by the 4th level. There is a good game here but right now it's more frustrating than it's worth

Has potential but is held back by bad decisions. You only have so many chances to get character shards to rank up per day, which can't even be refilled with cash. The PvP is pushed hard but is (imo) by far the worst part of the game. The premium currency is limited as hell, so you rarely get loot drops, which usually suck anyway. A lot of the inventory system is totally unexplained, and the balance between missions goes from do-able to completely impossible. The wave defense mode is fun tho.

The gameplay itself is fun and we'll done. However, as a new free to play player I found myself struggling to keep up with the power creep. The campaign forces you to use units from specific groups and the massive unit pool on the Gatcha makes it hard to get the duplicates needed to strengthen the required units. I spent 4 days grinding upgrade materials to get a minimal power increase. Be prepared to spend a long time grinding or ready to spend money.

The gameplay is fun right out of the gate, but you only have a few hours of content unless you pay. I'm fine with dropping real money on games I like, but the offerings weren't worth while. Nothing felt like it was going to 'open up' any new content short of spending 30+$ on new characters, and that would only be incremental. Until the monetization changes format, I would probably dodge this particularly abusive gacha bullet.

The grind. haven't even gotten to the point where energy is going to be a problem but it's coming quick and I know that's going to suck. can't bring myself to come back and play something that limits you like that. not to mention making the grind so terribly long that you aren't able to unlock content for probably a solid month. also way too many purchases.

Game feels good to play and looks wise looks awesome for a mobile game. But the characters are locked to specific campaigns for most of the game so you're stuck playing the same campaign for a long time with the same characters, unless you spend a big amount of money to directly unlock new characters to play other campaigns. The prices in the game are way too high for what they offerm. It's almos like your buying an expansion for a game if you're buying the characters to play more campaigns.

INCREDIBLY repetitive. Almost the entire game is grinding. It's structured in a way that is addictive, but in all the wrong ways. It can be fun, but it feels like you have to be on it all the time to make any progress. Even spending money makes very little difference on your progress. Changes to the game by the developers are slow. Progress in the game is slow. There are some insanely overpowered characters that make the game one-dimensional and boring. It's been disappointing.

This could have been a great game. Everything for that is there. Alas, they decided to make yet another fancy slot machine. You progress (way too easily) for a while, and eventually hit a wall. The only way to overcome is to replay the previous (not challenging) stages over and over and over, or throw money at it that completely trivializes the content. This could have been a great game, but it's not a game. Shame.

Tacitus is a decent time waster for the first five hours or so, but after that it's a complete slog. In the beginning you progress very quickly, but once you reach the last parts of the free campaign you'll hit a wall against a boss that will wipe your team instantly; beating him requires a huge grind which is time gated if you don't pay, which is a massive spike out of nowhere. I also still can't play Chaos, unless I spend even more time to randomly unlock two more characters, or pay $40 CAD.

Great game so far, but I hate having to click through 18 menus and a million buttons to collect gear and free things, plus I hate all the cash grab ads. I get it, every company wants to make money and it's a good game, but if there are less popups in a good game I am more willing to spend money than if it is pushed constantly. Also please make it either passively collect everything so there are less menus and buttons or one collect all available button or something, spend so much time in menus.

The game is great right now. Early gifts and quick progression through the 1st campaign. Haven't hit a grind wall yet. Lots of events to give you some variety. Update: Found it! The game is a slow power-crawl for heroes and their varied upgrades. Lots of different types of fights, but you will be fighting the same fight 15 times a day to stay relevant (arena battles). Energy system can go die. Wish there was more/deeper strategy. Clans aren't useful. Not my type of game (repetitous) uninstalled.

Typical gatcha. This could have been a really great game, but after about two days of fairly average game play you hit the pay wall. Run a mission with a 20% chance of dropping a token, until you get 80 tokens and can unlock a new character (about 400 times) or buy it now for cash. Progressing is gated in the same way, with level caps you can grind through (hundreds of runs) or just buy for cash. Please do better GW. Imagine how successful your games would be if they weren't pay to win trash

I must say, I had spent 5 years playing Star Wars: Galaxy of Heros and loved the game. However similar Tacticus is, it feels like it is a lot more versatile the that game. I have been playing for a few months now and I can feel the game pulling me into it. I really do enjoy this game, even without having any real experience in the Warhammer universe or lore. Not only is the game fun to play but the support for the game is fantastic. Quick responses on issues and very fair on issues. Great team!

So I put off getting this game for a while because I thought it would be some cash-grab using the Warhammer name but I've honestly had a ton of fun playing it. There's a variety of different mission types and objectives so it doesn't get stale, and it hasn't really pushed buying things on me. Honestly, I haven't gotten into the table top version, but if they had a section in the store to show at least what's available that would be cool.

Another PTP game, you will progress fine for the first few hours, then hit a brick wall and progression all but halts. Obvious there are many very expensive packages to buy that will allow you to continue to play, but expect to spend over $500. "Tokens" and "Energy" required to battle refill painfully slow, so the most you can F2P each day is about an hour.

If you're going to be such money hungry goblins, maybe create a game that doesn't crash every 15 minutes. Even if your game does crash maybe create a system where you can redeem the time sensitive items you need to fulfill certain game modes. But let's not kid ourselves here, just like everything games workshop does monetization comes before playability or customer

I wish this was not a PtW mobile game. It starts off with a bang: great gameplay experience, story, loot boxes coming in hot for free, steady upgrades, did I mention the gameplay really works? It's an excellent game. That is, as other reviewers have said, until you hit player level 11. After that, it slows to a crawl unless you get your wallet out. Extremely pay to win - no, pay to barely keep playing and pay a lot. Despite it, there is a very well done game under the PtW.

The game was extremely fun at first, but then the fun suddenly stopped. Leveling up your characters is too complicated and the game forces you to play other races in order to gather leveling materials for the characters you actually want to develop, which is an unusual approach but I don't like it. Also the terrain is low-res 2D which is bad for a tactical game. Otherwise there are tons of content to play so if you like Warhammer and turn based games you'll probably like it.

Fun gameplay, but too aggressive monetisation and few meaningful rewards mean it's impossible to unlock anything without spending hundreds of dollars, and the campaign is locked behind this pay wall as well as other game modes locked behind having x number of characters from a restricted list of factions. I don't want to play space marines, but my only other option if I want to continue to play is spend hundreds of dollars. If you want to play for free, I hope you like ultramarines

I played this for about a week. It became painfully clear that the game forces you into purchasing loot boxes to try to get a specific item that doesn't drop anywhere else in order to level your units. This isn't the worst crime, however. The worst is that the game just isn't very fun. All grind and no substance. I gave 2 stars since there is some good graphic design that deserves at least a nod. Hard pass.

Hi Devs! The game is filled with an incredible type of thrill especially the boss battles where the word "challenge" really comes into play. However, I really think you guys should cut down on the P2W materials. This isn't really something that throws the game into the dumpster, it's still great overall. Oh yeah, always remember, FOR THE EMPEROR!!

The game is great skirmish fun, but very stingy with the unlocks. It seems like you'd have to play for months and months just to get the faction you want. The graphics are well done, if a little cartoonish. Could do some better Grim-dark shading to give the Warhammer 40k feel. The gameplay is simple but strategy is still important. The upgrade system for the characters is a bit overly complicated, there are too many things to level up. Still, I recommend the game to scratch that 40k itch. 7.5/10

Really kinda disappointed, I was looking forward to a quick strategy came with the 40k flavor, which is definitely here, but quickly crippled by an intense pay wall. Fun gameplay and skin, for franchise lovers, but I got to about 60ish in Indomitus, when my team quickly lost steam. I then find out a lot of the upgrade bits for characters, will be found in drops /or/ locked behind 30$ campaigns. For a mobile game? Not really worth it , imo. Go buy Dawn of War instead

Fun but a hard grind. Low energy for missions so it's short gameplay time. It's expensive too. $30-$100 price for everything. I wouldn't mind dropping money on this game cause it's fun, but it's not worth it because you get 30-60min of gameplay a day depending if you play early and your energy recharges by dawn. I got the $10 season pass, but I until they lower prices and reward more energy, that's all I'm giving. Mainly as a donation for a decent game that I hope they improve the energy system.

Gameplay is decently fun and I haven't experienced many bugs or other issues, however I cannot recommend the game due to the sheer amount of microtransactions. From the moment you start playing, they practically beg you to spend money. It's annoying and ultimately will be the reason most people stop playing the game.

Good simple fun with a nice dose of tactical small unit play. Plenty of in game purchase stuff, but (so far) able to progress just fine without touching it. EDIT: So editing this and dropping the rating. Found the P2W jump lol. Baddies suddenly got a lot harder while simultaneously upgrading my guys became exponentially harder. Clear point where I'm now being told I need to fork out $$ to continue. Uninstalling.

This game is great and one of the better Warhammer titles on mobile. However it's completely undermined by its wonky micro transactions that make it hard to get any characters or power up your existing ones. Even as a paid player the cost is hard to swallow when you consider the fact you could go buy multiple sets of the actual GW models for less, which is wild since those have always been considered a pricier hobby. Level out the cost of the micro and this game will be fantastic.

Like others, thought this was a cash grab, but it's very well put together and paced. I like that it has several different game modes. Higher level characters are not out of reach if you don't want to spend the money and are patient. The grind may turn some away but its not too bad given how the board changes and enemies change based on terrain, abilities, etc. Overall, it's a great mobile platform game.

Resources needed for game are paywalled. Its a decent strategy game. But as is the modern trend, instead of charging 40-50 total for a game, you are required to spend about 60 a month for basic ongoing game play. It's not worth that much. Maybe if they dropped the premium sub to 1.99 and didn't lock the good cards as pay only it would be worth it. Anyway the PC Warhammer games are 100 times more detailed and only cost a flat one time fee. Play those.

Its a lot of fun, however the game feels like it's trying to attract only Warhammer 40k tabletop players. How you ask? Well the expectation of being able to drop 30-130 bucks to advance past a certain level is pretty obvious. So, much like the minis, if you can't afford to buy your way up I'd pass on this game.

Fun, but it gets old quick. One campaign is cool and all just up until the difficulty spike that requires you to grind up your characters and grind some more just to be able to chance a one-star victory. This at the end of the day is a game I play on the crapper, or while I'm passing time in a place where I can't play a real triple A game. It's not a game of the year experience worth paying 30 dollars to play the black legion campaign. Definitely tries to survive off the 40k brand clout.

It's a pay to win game after the first few days. EXTREMELY limiting in access to gameplay due to time restrictions (which makes no sense). Why would a game restrict gameplay time (without even options to pay to play longer) when ULTIMATELY it's a pay to progress game? The developers are either greedy or stupid. I reccomend NOT downloading unless you just want a few days of something new. After 4 days I'm deleting this poorly executed waste of time.

Fun gameplay, semi-tactical rpg. Horrible pay to win scheme. After about a day of playing you get hit hard with a pay wall. Need "energy" to play missions. Meaning there's about 15 minutes max a day you can play the game without spending money before that meter runs out making progress in the game completely redundant.

I have the utmost fun, intense, and addictive strategic game I've ever played on my mobile device. It's just have some issues with getting the upgrades for my characters' abilities and equipments. Another issue is that damn Tournament and the Arena mode that I've been competing against players that are extremely OP. I haven't even got most of my characters' experiences to rare or uncommon. Thus, makes this game an unfair and sometime rigged to cheat their customers. Please solve this issue.

Updated for 2025: I decided to try the game again. Yay, they've added dozens of characters since I last played. After a couple of weeks of grinding, it looks like I'll only need about 7 years to catch up to the for-pay players. Uninstall again ☹️ From 2023: I literally have 81 upgrades waiting across my characters and the fastest farming will take about 3 years to earn enough materials. Why does Snowprint insist on ruining great games with horrifyingly bad economies?

This is a fun game, and I love the world of 40k. The biggest downsides is this underlying push for transactions or paywalls to get the faction/race that I really want or through an obscene amount of grinding. It's simple to play and quick to pick up, and I enjoy the tactics of it. I wish it was better set up to either work for the factions I want or bring down those prices.

Game play is good, but many walls to progress game. I don't mind the grinding, but the jump in difficulty in the campaigns are ridiculous. Material required for upgrades behind the difficulty wall, with the tip of upgrading to win when you lose. Arena is broken in terms of difficulty/progression. Charge times for useful events is 12 hours each. Grinding is limited due to all the cool down times. Used to grinding games, but the restrictions in this game seem to follow GW real life mottos.

The game is ok but gets extremely stagnant and tedious. The gameplay is fun but does the bare minimum and forces you to use a specific set of characters if your F2P. I would've preferred if the game let choose a faction to start with because Warhammer 40k games are all about playing your favorites, and this game fails to cater to that. I don't want to play basic Ultramarines. I want to play guardsmen and Ravenguard. I understand using UM for a tutorial faction, but let us pick our starter.

I've never seen a game with such a lack of content. Recharge times take forever. Other than campaign mode you can't buy energy. Once you hit the wall in campaign mode what's the point of buying energy when all you can really do is find gear, and character shards. You want people to play more, and spend? Give them something to actually play, and spend money on.

Gameplay is simple and fun, but character acquisition - the core of the experience - is an RNG-gated slog that demands enormous grinding against low drop-rates. The Requisition system 'guarantees' a character if 10 hard-to-obtain resources are redeemed at once - but this includes characters you already have. I have now redeemed five such '10-drops' in a row without getting any of the 40+ characters I'm missing. It feels so bad that I regret buying the Season Pass. Back to F2P for me.

Game is okay, but too time gated. Character growth hid behind upgrade system that is chance-based and criminally slow. Actual play takes too much energy to be done regularly and maps are limited on number of times you can play a day. You will spend the most time in pvp, and the rewards for that aren't all that exciting. Tutorial is a big time waste and cannot be skipped if you want to log into an existing account on a new device.

Kinda fun tiny tactical battles, but ultimately just another smartphone game. Daily quests are a chore list, XPG progression ends up overshadowing tactical signifigance, and it uses quests to beg the player to sink time into all its game modes instead of just making those modes invitingly fun like real games do. Also, I'd hoped to get some of that famous 40K lore, but there's little to be found. And it takes up a lot of storage space.

Tough to get into without dedication. Getting any new characters are random drops/ collecting shards, so getting to new campaigns is quite the barrier (paywall removes this). I like how casual guilds can be, I just help out where I can and don't chat much. Arena can be a toss-up bc it automates your opponent's team. Quite relaxing, challenging at times and nuanced. Battle Pass worth it at the start of the season to advance your character pool so you'll need to shell out eventually

Increasingly pay oriented. Each single gacha draw is $3. They've started to paywall some newer characters and even then don't guarantee them because they're in a battlepass. No dedication to long time and paying customers either. Used a unique reset item they had given out and didn't get all the upgrades I was supposed to and support's answer was, "many other players have used that item without issue so you must be lying." Wallet warriors only and even then buyer beware!

LET ME start by saying I LOVE the 40K universe. This game has decent graphics and fairly easy to play. After about 35 to 40 levels it gets boring. The game doesn't have anything new except new playable characters but pretty much battles are the same. The arena battles are a joke I was always facing someone who had a squad that was way overpowered than my squad. SOME of the special abilities you could guess at while others you are clueless to unless you used them because there is no description.

Overall the gameplay is good, the events can be fun, and updates are frequent. The reason I am rating it at a two is because it is simply overly predatory with micro transactions. Some would claim it is pay to win, I have more of an issue with most of the purchases being gambles while others have unstated restrictions e.g. purchase daily rewards for a month except you do not receive them when you are unable to log in and those days get skipped. Might seem standard, feels scummy.

Changed my review. Can't recommend at all anymore. Game freezes all the time for me and my guild members and nobody seems to care to fix anything. I "lost" a lot of progress and I all but stopped caring anymore since I can hardly participate in most events due to freezing which counts as a loss even in fights I had all but won by the time the game froze. People fix your game, especially since a lot of the things you sell cost ridiculously high I would expect it at least to be playable...

Alright so I was tempted to rate this game higher but there are some GLARING issues. First of all, this game is pay to win. You can buy characters and this game feels very greedy. Second of all, character progression is slow. Like a character? Too bad. You'll need to unlock his 500 shards just to use him. Lastly because I can't fit more, resource gathering is a slog and a half. You can only play so much before the game begs you for more money. Not a great game, also, belisarious cawl is horrible

This game is fun. It IS interesting and also quite enjoyable/addictive. One thing becomes clear, however, which is that the developers clearly have no limits when it comes to engaging in a venal system of "Pay2Win". I understand the realities of modern app games, but they definitely take it to the next level. Purchases become essential for playing in any legitimate sense and even guilds are forbidden from trading upgrades higher than the common type.

It's a good tactics game. However p2w is a BIG deal here. Anytime you unlock a character you are hit with "deal" to pay to get another copy of them. This is one of those your going to need multiple copies to make them stronger. Drop rates are terrible, go look. I get p2w is always a thing in gachas but the disparity between paid and f2p is TOO high..There needs to be less you can buy in this game. No deals after every character unlock, and lower the price of 10 pulls to 2500.

A solid game with fun gameplay. But ultimately bogged down with too much monetization. Every activity has its own energy meter. Drop rates are way too low for some units, everything feels like a grind. Maybe ditch the energy cost for story, and up the drop on scrolls just a tiny bit. Events are great arena is a lot of fun, salvage is even cool. I just feel like you would rather us spend money than actually play. Also we need a friend list. Like an actial friend list.

good. it is entirely playable as free to play. it's a lot more playable if you spend like $10-30 annually. It would cost hundreds, if not a thousand USD+ to truly unlock all late game PVP and raid content, fast forward through most/all grinding, and have something near a complete collection. I do wish there was better value between spending a few bucks and jumping to a few hundred to see value. Spending $50 once in this game would be almost useless compared to spending $10.

Love 40k and enjoy tactical games. The main issue with this game is just getting the characters. I've bought a few packs, and I've farmed daily for a few characters. It just sucks the joy out of the game when I get on, and I will run my 10 run limit and pull 2 to 3 coins, and I'll need 250. If it was guaranteed 3 tokens, that would still take me 83 days. You should make getting the characters faster, then gearing them and staring them to be the grind, not both. That truly feelsbadman.

The tactical game is too diluted in the daily grind, in game payments and ads. You could spend hundreds of euros on that game and still not get where you want. Too bad cause when you get to play it, it is fun. The 3D models are awesome though it does feel like you are just using a 3D model viewer more than an actual game.

I must say once you get to approximately level 60, it becomes incredibly difficult up to that point it is incredibly easy. Most of my team is maxed out, I did this with out paying anything. but now my team will just get one shot within the first round. It's incredibly frustrating, as well even if you where to pay for the the things they just stop giving you to level up your caricatures attacks You may not get what you need You can't even use people from other factions you unlock. MONEY GRAB GAME

Fun game, but it has the same business model as Marvel Strike force. Need these types of players to play those matches. You can grind the same maps and take forever to unlock players for other maps, or you can give them entirely too much money. I stopped playing Strike force because it just requires too much money to play. I have a lot of stuff on there... they got me. this game won't do the same. I'll play until I hit the pay wall and move on. stop supporting these types of business models

Really love the art, really love the idea and campaigns (still love assault, raid and such but less intensively) but the game fun is greatly hindered by the pace at which you unlock the characters or the time needed to restore energy and tokens (for assault and such). Really putting the game as a "pay to win" or worst "pay to play" (where you don't pay once and then own the game) Let's see where it goes. May update the review consequently!

Decent game with pretty good game play, a lot of grind (to be expected) but tbh not too excessive. Main drawback: I think the servers are made of cardboard, as we get locked out for a day at a time pretty regularly, sometimes twice a week, with no warning because the game can't connect. To the extent that I'm struggling to do the battle pass because I can't get enough game time.

Fun game, i really like the warhammer 40k universe. but after 1-2 days you really hit the paywall hard and have to grind like mad to progress. you have to do the eays stages oder and over to be able to finally get a hard stage done until you hid teh next barrier. Could have been a really great game, but the price of the different packages are really insane and you can't grind everything.

Sorry everyone.... This is another freemium game that could have potential but all they want is money... yet again energy/wait/gems . As of the moment of this post it would cost 300$ plus to "maybe" unlock all characters then even more rare tokens which would easily reach the 1000$ mark if you wanted to level them up by paying cash. I wouldn't recommend anyone putting money in to this unless you just like wasting it.. which in that case this game is for you.

The game has potential. The game suffers in 2 main areas. Lack of playable characters and repetitive gameplay. Both can be fixed, I'd love to see the game expanded to include some of the lesser loved factions in 40k like the Adeptus Mechanicus. The game has a few different styles of game modes but they all blend together. With around 40 unlockable characters it seems unfinished relying on luck or spending real money to upgrade your troops. I'd rate it higher if some changes are made.

It's...OK. very great design and concept on the tactical rpg style but after a while there is not that much to do. It's an Energy based game so once you run out you can't really progress any further, and the timer is fairly long to recover fully. With more development I would love to play this on a console with a decent storyline and bigger maps. Add in a little more character customization and your golden. Until then... meh

All in all. Very nice game. The cash grab could be a bit cheaper. I don't mind paying a few bucks for a constantly updated game with a big community. Also a lots of free codes with good drops. For a free game absolutely fine. Spent many hours so far and dropped also a coin for it. Might be more if a bit adjusted. Learn a bit about lore, community and many more things from the 40k universe. Good job, always aim higher. 4.7/5

Actually a tolerable mobile game and is a better Warhammer 40k game on mobile. I tend to stray far away from mobile games with Warhammer 40k and yes they do stick micro transaction offers on you everytime you get back to the menu but unless you really have nothing else to spend your money on or you're impatient, you can enjoy the game at a steady pace. I'm not much of a PvP guy so I couldn't tell you about it but overall it is a decent mobile game. Just maybe not so many "Buy this!" Prompts.

After the recent update, I have lost absolutely all of my progress. I would like to know if there is any available way to reclaim it. An absolutely five star game, I'm just upset at the loss of my progress thus far. I was also very close to unlocking Athena, which I am very disappointed I have lost progress on. Please let me know if I can regain anything :(

Wanna play a game that wiggles awesome characters in front of you and doesn't let you get them without spending cash? Oh, you don't? Then pass on this shameful cash grab. Less than 24 hours in, they have barely trickled any scrolls for character pulls, and when they do, I hope you like getting materials for upgrades instead of new heros... what they offer in abundance, a sprawling list of available in-game purchases. May the Heritics who made this suffer.

Overall gameplay is great, really requires you to factor in ranges, terrain, and where you move. Only issue is that the non-campaign modes take so long to regenerate, and so resources take forever to collect. It should take 3-4 hours to have another go at the other modes, not 16 hours. Prices in the store are also too high, and don't offer much value for what you pay.

Calling this a strategy game is completely misleading. The only thing that matters in this game is the level of your characters and how much they've been grinded up to a higher level. One attack that will do no damage to one of your characters will insta kill another character that's only a few levels lower. Due to that most maps are your guys being invulnerable and a snore or them getting one-shotted on the very first attack.

The game is fun. The only problem is, I paid for a premium battlepass, which worked initially. It stopped working the next day, not allowing me to claim rewards. I messaged them, and they seemingly fixed it, but still some portions of premium rewards in other sections won't work, saying I have to pay as if I hadn't already. I paid 10 dollars for the premium battlepass, and I don't think I should have to contact their support multiple times for poor implementation. Oh well.

Game progression is a 10% angle. Game difficulty rises at an 80% angle. Takes months to unlock or level up characters to 4* or more if you arnt spending actually money and raid tokens?!! Game has raid token to do auto finish on campaign missions. They quickly run out. Its a shame. Game has great modes and mechanics. I honestly would have bought the game as a one off payment and have realistic progression rather than these multi in game purchases that all quickly add up to over €100.

Just like their miniatures, that are way over priced, this game hits a pay wall. They care not for the little guy trying to have fun playing their games. They only care for those who have money to burn. You hit a pay wall eventually. Not being able to progress without spending. It is sad seeing this since I recently got into Warhammer. Won't buy another miniature and definitely won't spend in this game with it's blantent EA like microtransactions.

like the game, but so not beginner friendly. been playing for a couple of weeks now all events you feel vastly underpowered. first 2 missions are ok, but you will hit a wall fast. hard to get resources because on top of everything it's an energy based game. so you are very limited to get your resources and upgrades unless ofc pay for it. am feeling frustrated and lost because I feel I am so limited to catch up.

Everything about the game is great, but We should be able to play Campaign offline, but more importantly, there should be a setting to reduce the graphics and animation quality for smoother gameplay because it's very slow on my phone and causes my phone to overheat everytime I play it. This has made it very inconvenient to play. Please consider this.

Overall, I've been enjoying the game off and on for years. Some of these events, however, seem... scamy?. Tournament arena. The odds of you going second and winning are astronomically low. Some of these campaigns have me fighting gold guys in the silver campaign area. It's like you don't want us to progress or do well... unless you buy the "special" campaign box to progress. Some of the stuff you do has driven away one of the biggest content creators of the game. Do better.

The first few hours are good, but this game is aggressively monetized if you want to advance to any degree beyond the early game. To its credit, the game is upfront about it, and clear about what you get for actual money, but it is still very blatant and aggressive. Good graphics and not many bugs as far as I've seen. Gameplay is straightforward and functions well.

As 40k Mobile Games go, this is one of the better ones. Gameplay is fun, visuals look great, a surprising amount of content. It is aggressively monetized, but so far it seems generous enough to not just immediately hit a pay wall. Update: I hit the pay wall. And boy is it a rough one. Best you can hope for is improving inch by inch, and if you wanna buy in? The pricing is insane, costing about $25 for one 10 pull. There's still a great game under all this, but right now it's still shackled.

It is fun enough until you bottom out on collecting characters at level 12, which only takes a day or two to achieve. It is your basic pay to win scheme. Maps are very, very small. prices are way overpriced. to buy a character pack, they want $30. if you collect one in the pack then want to buy, it is $20. they think a mobile game character is worth $10 each. that is a problem when inflation and the lower class playing this have trouble paying rent... a few adjustments would make it great

There is a lot I enjoy about the game, but overall, there are a few glaring predatory tactics that detract from gameplay. The wait times for consumables (i.e. energy, tokens, etc.) to refill are absurd. The use of energy and tokens to gamble for possible upgrade material to progress characters after you have fully completed a mission is frustrating. If you are going to limit the number of times you can re-attempt a mission, then the raid tokens are redundant and reduce gameplay.

I really REALLY want to love this game more. The problem is, the difficulty ramps up REALLY fast, and you hit a wall. So you're either left playing a couple of battles a day hoping to be able to upgrade your team, or just repeatedly smash your head against a brick wall. I would also appreciate some choices. You are pretty much stuck with the same team, with no ability to switch members based on the situation (outside of arena). It's so close to being great, but so far.

Seems like a simplistic pay to play cash grab game. Maps are small, mechanics are basic, energy required to play is timed, battles are repetative, it does get more complex as you progress but progression is limited. If you have nothing better to do, it is a good time killer, but there are MUCH better things to do and far better games to play to kill time in a person's life. Even though it is a free download, I still feel like i wasted my money for time and data to download. Do not recommend.

Very fun for the first little while, but honestly there's not that many tactics in tacticus. A few levels after the app prompts you to rate and review it (I can only assume this is on purpose) the enemies start to insanely outlevel your characters, and you run into necrons that duplicate themselves every turn. The only way to win is to take out all of those units on the first turn, and the only way to do that is to grind your characters forever... or pay to upgrade them. Definitely a pay to win.

Fun but excessively limited. I get the need for an energy system, really, but literally everything is tied to some type of timer, and there are so many opportunities for the game to be more. I'd love to just play skirmish missions. Or figure out how to beat a mission without rewards and without blowing all my energy to advance. There's no practice, no practice. Just waiting. Basically i want to play the game more but can't, because everything is about rank and progress.

It's... okay. Visuals are great, gameplay is fun, there's a lot to like, but it's virtually impossible to progress or even PLAY the game without considerable financial investment. Energy system depletes very quickly and charges slowly. Many fun alternative game modes exist, but they are on even longer cooldowns still, and unlocking new characters will probably take months of free play (or a macrotransaction). Can't recommend in its current state, but there's a lot of potential here.

Game looks good, however the UI is basically unusable on my device (Note 9) because of the location of the main buttons lining up with the home button. I'd have to make additional changes to my settings to make this game work, which unfortunately is more work than I'd be willing to do for a mobile game. The AI control of unit movement can be terrible at times. Moving units into less than optimal positions when making an attack. I also don't like how often I'm hounded to spend money.

Absolutely love this type of gameplay; reminds me of the old Age of Empires game for DS. Cool music, colorful UI, and solid gameplay. Edit: Over time, the way the cash shop pushes itself became very grating. Character leveling feels very mechanical, only having different art for items. They don't feel like they mean anything. Just keep clicking on things that say they're active and that's pretty much it. Gets stale quickly and feels like you hit a wall.

Fun game when you're able to play it. Everything you do is locked behind a time wall, and you don't get nearly enough energy to play the game. You're even capped on how many times you can refill your energy per day. The game also crashes, and if you're in a battle, it will consume that token you used to get into the battle, then you're stuck with a 14 hour timer to get it back.

It is what it's supposed to be, an awesome game. It's fun, a little graphic heavy, hey I dig it, and not completely pay to win. Day 1 baby! Edit: Day 2. Hit level 11 yesterday; instantly hit with the hard pay-wall. All top competitors have dumped cash, upwards of $30.00. Doesn't sound like a lot until you consider it's a mobile game. And physical miniatures? It's one or the other, and if prices don't start really coming down for plastic I have to put together and paint, I'm about done. Not sorry

A lot of fun at the beginning to get you hooked, you get many rewards and new heroes, and then, like most mobile games, you hit the pay wall, I don't mind spending cash to support the devs, but with this game, you'd need to continuously spend A LOT of money. Also, the AI is dumber than a rock, if you just select enemies to attack them and don't position your heroes before doing so, the game will place them in the worst possible place even if several better options are available.
No AI, No Ads (unless you go searching for one). All around fun game. Sometimes I wish it was a little bit more difficult but that's me being picky.

Overall a good game. The monetization is weird. You don't get much bang for your buck, but spending money isn't required. The game feels more worthwhile as s Free to player than spending money. Progression can be s little slow. But the core gameplay is fun. There are multiple modes which bring nice variety. The characters also have a nice variety and play in very different ways. Definitely worth trying, especially if you like 40k. Hopeful for the future.

Just a money grind, Claims things are done by chance, but they are very clearly just geared to make you buy as much as possible. For example, things that guarantee a new character that are diffcult/expensive to get just give you the same characters you already have repeatedly, but you're welcome to buy them! Ridiculous. Terrible, boring dialogue writing in the story campaigns
Love the machanics, just wish it was more like the tabletop with dice rolls (for attacks, successes, saves etc.). Other than that great game. Just waiting on expansion.

Way better than I anticipated. tactics are legit(if a little too easy to cheese in the arena), characters have very distinct and unique feel. Good base for sure which makes the monetization really weird. everything is insanely expensive but kinda unnecessary. On top of that, the timers for anything but the campaign are insanely long. 12 hours for resource farms, and even an hour for arena, and many of your dailies require them. So close to great but the grind gets tedious.

The game is a good representation for 40K fans; a very expensive p2w model, and meta sort of pigeon holes a few target squads, but overall as a f2p player there is a lot of fun. There are many campaigns, lots of units, heaps of events and always something to do. Whilst the game is generally fun, you do feel the grind. Lots of people leave and come back. I'll probably be one of those.

when app crashes during a game it takes away your token but does not give you any reward or count as having played that mode. when they sell tokens and energy this should only deduct if the game plays as intended.

The perfect game for millionaires, not a millionaire, well I got bad news. You can play this cash sucking pos, or eat and pay rent, but not all three. Tactius in Chinese must mean, "sukka." The game starts well, until you hit the end of chapter 3 that's where they want a review, and reward you with suddenly making it harder than you can ever beat unless of course you buy special characters that cost 20 bucks then 40, 80 ect. Plan to spend around 100 a week. And it really isn't that fun.

The visuals are great but the flow of the entire UI is very clunky. Haven't played long enough to truly do the F2P aspect. However, based on initial numbers, this a money trap. I buy into a number of gacha style games but this is rough. I got severe P2W wibes. It's over the top shoving "buy this or buy that" aspect which really put me off. Especially since it was from the very start. Feels like a normal gacha game only on the 40K universe which doesn't say much.

I've been a huge fan of Warhammer 40k since the late '80s when I got into the miniatures. I've been a huge fan of the PC and mobile games since they first started. What lowered this from a 5-star to a 1-star rating is the game stops EVERY 10-15 minutes, forcing me to reload and killing my momentum in the mission(s) I was working on. Furthermore, even though I've contacted Tech Support nothing has been done to address/correct the problem

Was fun for a little, then the waiting and lack of balance forces you to either waste a ton of time to get a new character or pay. Also, who loves it when a game makes you wait to play?? Gave up when the 10 requisition drop that says "guaranteed character" didn't give me a character, or even enough to level up a new character. Screw this

In the grimdarkness of the future, there is only grind. Like every other mobile game out there, the game will shower rewards on you for the first few days to get you hooked, then prepare to grind after that. However, unlike many of the complaints here, I actually really like the long mission reset timers and energy - I don't want to spend 4 hours a day grinding, if I can get everything done in an hour I don't feel like the game is wasting my time compared to a lot of other games out there.
I really like the fact that starting out I have divergent paths. Most games start out so step by step linear that it might as well be someone elses playthrough.

Re-skin of Rivengard with great looking WH40k chars. I got bored of it, but it was entertaining briefly. Didn't discover significant strategy element, battlefields are very small, lots of very similar combats, lots of things to arbitrarily level up. A gacha game with premium and in-game currency, tons of grinding options, turn-based combat system with no autoplay & very little choice for players. Also feels like a P2W -- but wasn't for me bc I ain't payin'!

It was okay. the game felt a bit rough and it feels like they are forcing payment in front, so it feels like a money grab. The idea is okay but the execution is poor-rough. The number of available character is okay but it lacks the "interesting pull" for us to grind for chsracters. The main thing that annoy me is how rough (bad) the game felt. During training I scrolled on character draw menu, and when the game order me to draw chara, it just stuck because I was scrolling to the bottom. 6/10 imo
Haven't played enough yet but so far pretty good. Obviously you are getting hit with annoying offers for better equipment and troops but pretty good simple strategy game.

Advertised heavily as an RPG, this game has nothing to do with an RPG. It is a heroes strategy game. At first, it's quite fun but quickly turns into a tedious repetitive grind. The "arena" match-making is terribly flawed, where it pits player vs player in simulated head-to-head battles. The system tries to match up your army against impossible-to-defeat enemy armies that are hundreds, if not thousands, of times more powerful. You end up spending hundreds of gems just refreshing the matchups.

A great set of strategy mechanics buried under an incredibly onerous and obnoxious progression system. GOOD: The strategy gameplay itself is well executed with a fantastic variety of characters, abilities, stages and enemies. Gameplay actually has depth. The look slickly nails that pulpy 40k aesthetic. BAD: You'll spend more time navigating menus than you will playing the game because there's so many currencies in progression systems to keep track of.

I've been playing this for a while now and had to leave a review because I can honestly say this game can be enjoyed as a F2P without spending a penny. Good drop rate for new characters. There is a grind and the energy limit is not enough at times. Unlimited energy events on occasion would be nice. But ultimately the game has to make money somehow too. I've never been a Warhammer fan, but I've really enjoy this game. Good TBS. Kudos to the Devs for not being too greedy.

The gameplay itself is really solid, and the diversity of character abilities makes team formation interesting and strategic. That said, I do have a couple things i hope get ironed out later. Notably, when I finally earned enough premium currency to do some summons, I pulled a strong character from a Chaos faction. Unfortunately, I can't use him anywhere right now due to missions restricting which factions' can be deployed. Great game otherwise, though!

Gameplay is alright, but quickly becomes grindtastic to get gear you need to level up characters in order to progress. or of course you can pay real money for any of the gazillion "micro transaction" packs shoved down your throat. The arena matchmaking is an absolute joke too; most of the time all three opponents are 2, 10, or literally over 400 times my power rankings! It's ok, but I will certainly uninstall before long as progress slows to a snail's pace with find and waiting for timers.

WOW! After having a lot of fun for all of 3 hours. This game turned into any other PTW game, except worse. You need tokens to play side games and it takes HOURS to recharges them. Unless you pay money you get stuck in the first chapter of the main campaign within a few rounds. After winning all PVP chests there is literally zero point to playing anymore. I'm extremely bummed because I really enjoy this game type and absolutely love Warhammer. Chalk this up to another greedy developer.🖕

Changing my review after playing for a long while. Don't bother with this game unless you have deep pockets. Every hero is locked behind a paywall event. There is no way to unlock said hero unless you pay for random pulls. The drop rates are abysmal. It's really too bad because the game can be great if not for the greedy tactics. Snowprint will no longer be receiving a dime from me.

Genuinely one of the worst experiences I've had. The gameplay itself is super barebones. There's a constant drop feed of popups telling you about "special deals" trying to get you to pay unreasonable prices for fee in game items. And finally, you've got this "energy" system that dissuades you from even playing the game when you want. Progress is painfully slow, but the game is very easy, so you end up just playing the same missions over and over on a painfully monotonous grind fest.
Amazing use of characters and great models, I love the abilities, and the many different ways you can play. Great game.

The game is limited in a few ways, levels can only be completed 10 times a day, characters need tokens to unlock/upgrade and those are random drops, you can only play certain game modes once every few hours, etc. With all this going on, why THE HECK is there an energy system on top of it! I'm already barely allowed to play, so why limit me even more? It's a great game, it has some really good ideas, but that paywall is rough.

This game is fun, and has its moments for sure. But if you don't buy anything, you won't get very far. I noticed that once I got past the third Necron boss, materials started dropping less, and missions got expotentially more difficult. The game has potential, but it's less about tactics and more about reaching number thresholds to beat levels.

Can be fun. Drawn back a bit by design choices. Some units take forever to build; pre sure resources are scant purposely to incite purchases. Battles can easily go from half way to victory, to utter defeat regardless of builds, and the difficulty on some raids, etc, feel manufactured. I think abilities should be overhauled for many units. Crates&Reqs need to be increased, or demands reduced. Farming is 95% of gameplay without your wallet. Otherwise, alright game.

It's a fun game and premise; definitely follows the formula of Star Wars Galaxy of Heroes to a point. If you like that game or Warhammer you'll probably at least get some enjoyment of this game. My biggest gripe however is that every player MUST start as Ultramarines at the beginning and then slowly farm to unlock characters from any other faction. It would be best if we could choose one at the beginning and then farm for the rest. Really just wanted to play orks, and I still have none.

Played the game for about an hour and got 4 ads to buy in game currency or in game characters. That's about 1 per 15 minutes of play. That's too many disruptive ads. To be clear these aren't the usual "video" ads. I typically don't mind ads in free games as I understand you need to make money but I don't like when my game is getting interrupted anytime I was to go upgrade my character or switch to new mission. If you can ignore the interruption of ads every few minutes then this game is fun.

Great visuals and initially very fast and fun. Game slows down fast and really digs into trying to get you to pay for stuff. You have to be really paitent for everything. There are way to many requirements to upgrade characters. The games needs to keep free players engaged better. Chosmetics are the only thing that should be "paid" for in games nowadays.

Haven't needed to pay for anything game has been nice with the energy output,though I'm only doing 4 because I thought you would be able to stack requisition from mission 19 2nd necron however it only gave me one after I grinded The mission. However If you go and open it after each time replaying it you should be able to get each one, other than that I'm enjoying the game greatly. Hope they add the lamenters someday.

Holy pay wall that hits quicker than most. Should change the name to Gatekeeper 40,000. Everything relates in a way that holds you back from getting too strong in one area without the other 40,000 currencies worth of upgrades following. Ordinance and Blackstone rates are pretty bad, didn't get enough of either to pull enough to judge draw odds. Be ready to pay up for extended play, otherwise it's good for 2-5 days of free fun depending on your patience.

It's pretty good for a 40k game but it's way over priced on every single layer. The battlepass at 9.99 is massively overpriced for only lasting 30 days, and other chapter's costing $30 is just laughable, you can unlock them for free (I think) but it takes forever the way you have to do it, and before the devs point out that the price drops for each character unlocked, even when you get down to only needing 1 more character to unlock a campaign, it's still massively overpriced.

I find the grind to just get anywhere has overwhelmed my drive to play about 10mins after I start it up everytime. I've had the same characters for a month and I just don't care to try and get more anymore. I can't get into the game because the beginning is so bland and repetitive. There's so many types of battles and events but just don't seem to care because I don't see the point in getting into it any further. Good inspiration, terrible execution.

Interesting and attention-grabbing for sure, good dynamic yet simple combat. Good animations and style. The only problem I'd have with this game is that, like any other mobile game nowadays, is that it seems to be too focused on getting you to buy things instead of investing time in the game. But again, this is something you can rarely escape from a free mobile game title. At least this one is enjoyable and seems to be worthwhile so far.

Nothing like the PC game, don't be mislead by title. Game is free to play for 3 hours after which (once the free loot boxes run out) you have to pay to play (and p2w in every event). For context, you need 5 chars for a team, maxing a single character costs over $10k. You also need different teams for different battles. Overall, it's great to burn time on (you have 10 mins of content per day after the first 3 hours). Cheers

This has the bones of a good strategy and Warhammer casual game. But all the hallmarks of a terrible freemium money waster. You will feel like you're getting lots of resources at first and then hit a wall where it starts really trying to dig into your wallet. And do you want to play free with your favorite faction? Lol, you'll need to beat them >800 times to unlock them first.

Once you get through the tutorial, the games economy comes to a screeching halt. I feel like i haven't made progress in days. On top of that i haven't been able to play at all today because the game tells me im not connected to the internet while my phone tells me I am. There is an event I cant participate in because I dont have enough of a specific type of unit, and the only missions that get you items you need to upgrade your characters can only be played 1-2 times per day.
Preliminary rating. So far so good. Lots of ads and p2w opportunities early on.

This could be a very good game. Unfortunately, it's not. Character development is very limited, unless you pay for it big time. Anything except the basic ultramarines is next to impossible to progress. On higher levels, it gets even worse. Guild raid rewards are trash, pvp also, except if you are in top ten. Very disappointing, sadly.

For some reason right now with current update the game will crash when clicking on almost anything. Will update review when this is fixed obviously a bug of some kind, game will crash when starting a mission and still charge you. Maybe don't make everything based on spending money and you would have a larger player base and hence more people to spend money on the game. Please fix the crash bug very sad to have to wait another 151/2 hours for a token I didn't get to use.

The game was nice, but with the new "event campaign" the time needed to get anything in the game has become too much for me to enjoy. This is a mobile game, so i expect to put in to it 30-45 minutes in average a day in total, but as it stands in need to sink hours upon hours daily to get anywhere. Also the change to guild raids mean that if i can't access the game for a day i get locked out of all rewards.

Not bad but def hard monetization. It starts out pretty easy and enjoyable, however about halfway through the second quest section it's clear they game is hard monetized. The screens are crowded feeling and def push for you to buy units with real money. If you keep playing its mostly a pick up for maybe 10 mins and then come back tomorrow. Maybe it'll improve and be a bit more cleaned up and less cluttered but for me I can't keep playing after about a week.

-1 right off the bat because says offline but you can't do any missions without being connected, just looking at your collection and somehow the store. Raid tokens are stingy, and the game bombard you with energy for the first 4 hours before slowing to a crawl where you need to grind for so much stuff to level characters re-running levels. No real tactics, just level characters. There are some cool terrain stuff, but it is not as important as level (except for some spots unable to melee).

Most predatory gacha game I have encountered where you spend most of your time watching ads (many of which crash the game and thus give no reward), yet the developers seem to not want to address these issues

The game can be fun but like most 40k games, greedy and cheap with the gatcha. Lots of grinding, much content behind unit unlock walls. Expect pricey micros. PvE/raiding has faction mission requirements, so v. limited team building. You'll be using the first 5 units you get with no other options for a long, long time. There only 1 server, have fun competing against people who've been playing for years. Still the same 2025.

Besides the smack in the face pay to win elements (pay to play too sadly unless you just get ungodly lucky with it's gacha system, as only one story mode of the game are you given what you need freely). It is and can be a fun game, but having played since release to now, some of the unnannounced changes have bugged me quite a bit. Including a provable drop rate decrease which has kneecapped my progression even while paying, just too greedy, 2/5

At first I was interested but maps become a one way or fail mission. Gets old really fast, a challenge is one thing but the game makes you have to play every move right or you lose. Not much to learn from your mistakes and gets aggravating fast. Worst part is even when unlocking characters first few are ment to be unlocked first, which is fine but when you get new characters you can't switch them out during the campaign. Reason for two stars is very add free beside micro transactions.

If I'm being honest in the beginning the game was pretty darn fun, some of the levels where a bit to easy, and some where a fun kinda change, but now it's just getting straight up difficult without the fun, and I dont feel like I should need to have to pay to get a character or upgrades to get to something, least not 40 some odd dollars, I know you gotta make money some how tbh I'd be fine if you had me watch ads from time to time then something like what you have going on.

No. Yet another grindy, limited content gatcha game. The pay wall starts in the fourth part of the first campaign. Like Galaxy at War, one of the most predatory mobile games to exist, you don't even earn characters - you earn pieces of characters. Then, they're gated behind upgrades, which you also have to grind or pay for. All this to play a poorly designed, hex-based strategy-lite game that shares an IP with 40k but not much else. I'd have suffered the game more if it could be an auto-battler.

After playing for total 5 to 10 hours there is nothing to do accept arena. Charactera become weak in the ultramarine campaign and you cant do anything really. This is a trap to make you pay money and play other campaigns. I love warhammer and will play the game regardless. The game is new and content will come so i gave it 3 stars but it can be 5 stars easily.

Rivengard but 40k, start with a shock-based dps, then get a tank who can summon more allies, then a sharpshooter with a special ability that knocks back enemies, etc. Obviously both snowprint so I'm not surprised the UI and combat are so similar but I do wish the characters were at least unique, or that you got the same archetypes in a different order than in Rivengard.

After a couple of days of playing, it's not bad at all. The fighting is fun and more strategic than most mobile games, by a large margin. The downside comes in the microtransactions, character unlocks, and pvp. This game is HEAVILY Pay to win. Additionally, they use the standard 10-ticket "gacha" system but 10 pulls average out to around $30, in which you may only get a handful of shards when you need hundreds to pull the character. If you want to spend money it's great. if not, forget PvP

Lovely artwork, great skill animation, but at this point (2h a day for a couple of months) it became obvious that, unless I spend money, progress is unnoticeably slow. The arena is ruled by players several times stronger, so your only option is either reroll until you find someone your level, or lose until you run into your equal or lesser. And while I do appreciate that I can grind for base characters it takes SO long to do so. I play games as a hobby, I don't want them to be a second job.

It's mobile gotcha shlock. It's good shlock, but shlock none the less. Three currencies to level a character, only one of which actually drops playing 95% of the game. Bosses that make you wish "If only my character would level so I could actually counter this" as you look at five characters with 20/500 tokens. If you see a discount hero, avoid it, my "great deal" was garbage. Enjoy the 5 bucks you got out of me, cause you ain't getting more.

A fun game that the developers won't let you play. The core 40k tactics combat is fun, but as you progress the enemies get harder, and the only way to win is to grind materials. Sadly the energy you use to grind materials is also used to play the battles, so once you are through the first few days of playing you'll end up spending days only grinding so you can be powerful enough to actually play through a few battles. This makes it constantly disappointing.
best tactical game for the phone, and a damn good warhammer game

Very good experience from a free-to-play aspect. Advertisements are kept to a minimum and only there if you want some extra playtime or want to refresh the item shop. Good community from discord and the guilds you can join in-game. Steep learning curve though which means well thought out game mechanics. 6+ months into having this game and it still takes a considerable amount of my screen time. Good story telling using the campaign missions. Limited time events every few weeks that last 1-2 weeks

Almost great game. Other than the fact that there are some battles that you can do LITERALLY NOTHING. I just played 3 battles where I got to move my characters and then watch them die without literally doing a thing because, of course, the other guy has a full team of epic or legendary characters ready to one or two-shot my team of starters, which I didn't choose.
